title.zh: 卷二十四 志第十四 職官
title.raw: 卷二十四 志第十四 職官 Volume 24 Treatises 14: Government Service

sentences.zh: 《書》曰：「唐虞稽古，建官惟百。

translations.literal: The Book of Documents says: "Tang and Yu examined antiquity; they established offices numbering only one hundred.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Documents says: "When Tang and Yu looked back to antiquity, they created no more than a hundred offices.

sentences.zh: 」所以獎導民萌，裁成庶政。

translations.literal: " By this means they encouraged and guided the common people, and brought order to every branch of government.
translations.idiomatic: That was how they encouraged the people and gave shape to the affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 《易》曰：「天垂象，聖人則之。

translations.literal: The Book of Changes says: "Heaven hangs forth images; the sage takes them as his model.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes says: "Heaven displays signs; the sage patterns himself on them.

sentences.zh: 」執法在南宮之右，上相處端門之外，而鳥龍居位，雲火垂名，前史詳之，其以尚矣。

translations.literal: " Law sat to the right of the Southern Palace; the chief minister took station beyond the Duan Gate; the Bird and Dragon offices held their posts, cloud and fire lending their names—earlier histories spell this out in detail, and the dignity of it is plain.
translations.idiomatic: Justice lay to the right of the Southern Palace; the chief minister waited beyond the Duan Gate; bird and dragon offices held rank with cloud and fire as their emblems—prior histories lay it out clearly, and the grandeur speaks for itself.

sentences.zh: 黃帝置三公之秩，以親黎元，少昊配九扈之名，以為農正，命重黎於天地，詔融冥於水火，則可得而言焉。

translations.literal: The Yellow Emperor instituted the ranks of the Three Dukes to stay close to the black-haired masses; Shaohao paired the Nine Hu bird-names with the office of director of agriculture; Chong and Li were charged with Heaven and Earth; Zhu Rong and Ming were charged with fire and water—these arrangements can indeed be described.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow Emperor created the Three Dukes to draw near to the people; Shaohao aligned the Nine Hu titles with agricultural oversight; Chong and Li received Heaven and Earth; Zhu Rong and Ming received fire and water—and such patterns can be put into words.

sentences.zh: 伊尹曰：「三公調陰陽，九卿通寒暑，大夫知人事，列士去其私。

translations.literal: Yi Yin said: "The Three Dukes harmonize yin and yang; the Nine Ministers watch cold and heat; grand officers understand human affairs; ranked officers rid themselves of selfishness.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Yin said: "The Three Dukes harmonize yin and yang; the Nine Ministers track the seasons; grand officers attend to human affairs; ranked officers put private interest aside.

sentences.zh: 」而成湯居亳，初置二相，以伊尹、仲虺為之，凡厥樞會，仰承君命。

translations.literal: " When Cheng Tang ruled from Bo, he first created two chancellors and appointed Yi Yin and Zhong Hui to them; on every critical matter they looked upward to receive the ruler's commands.
translations.idiomatic: When Tang of Shang made Bo his seat, he first set up two chancellors—Yi Yin and Zhong Hui—and on every pivot they carried out the sovereign's will.

sentences.zh: 總及周武下車，成康垂則，六卿分職，二公弘化，咸樹司存，各題標準，苟非其道，人弗虛榮。

translations.literal: Altogether, when King Wu of Zhou stepped down from his chariot to rule, Cheng and Kang handed down norms; the Six Ministers divided duties; the Two Dukes spread transformation; each office kept its place and measure; if it were not the proper Way, people did not vainly seek glory.
translations.idiomatic: Under King Wu and the models left by Cheng and Kang, the Six Ministers split the labor, the Two Dukes carried royal influence abroad, every bureau had its charter, and no one claimed idle honors without the right conduct.

sentences.zh: 貽厥孫謀，其固本也如此。

translations.literal: They left plans for their descendants; thus they secured the foundation.
translations.idiomatic: They anchored the dynasty by planning for generations yet unborn.

sentences.zh: 及秦變周官，漢遵嬴舊，或隨時適用，或因務遷革，霸王之典，義在於斯，既獲厥安，所謂得其時制者也。

translations.literal: When Qin altered the Zhou offices and Han followed the Ying-clan precedent, sometimes adapting to the times, sometimes shifting with practical needs—the norms of hegemons and kings lay herein; once stability was gained, this is what is called obtaining timely institutions.
translations.idiomatic: Qin refashioned Zhou's bureaucracy; Han largely kept Qin's frame while tweaking it for the moment—the logic of strong rule was there—and stability meant institutions matched their age.

sentences.zh: 四征興於漢代，四安起于魏初，四鎮通於柔遠，四平止於喪亂，其渡遼、淩江，輕車、強弩，式揚遐外，用表攻伐，興而復毀，厥號彌繁。

translations.literal: The Four Expeditions arose in Han; the Four Pacifications began at the start of Wei; the Four Garrisons reached outward to soothe the distant; the Four Peace offices ended with turmoil and disorder; as for Crossing-the-Liao, River-Fording, light chariot, and strong crossbow—they displayed might afar and signaled campaigns—raised up and then abolished, their titles grew ever more numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Han invented the Four Expeditions; Wei at its outset the Four Pacifications; Four Garrisons stretched toward distant peoples; Four Peace posts vanished when chaos returned. Epithets like Crossing-the-Liao, River-Fording, light chariot, and strong crossbow brandished force beyond the borders for campaigns—created, scrapped, then multiplied until the catalogue grew tangled.

sentences.zh: 及當塗得志，克平諸夏，初有軍師祭酒，參掌戎律。

translations.literal: When the house at Dangtu achieved its ambition and subdued the Central Plain, there first appeared the army adviser libationer, who jointly handled military regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Cao regime triumphed and pacified the heartland, it introduced the army adviser libationer to share oversight of military law.

sentences.zh: 建安十三年，罷漢台司，更置丞相，而以曹公居之，用兼端揆。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Jian'an, the Han terrace ministers were abolished; the chancellor was reinstated, and Lord Cao held it, thereby combining the highest civil authority.
translations.idiomatic: In 208 Cao Cao abolished the old Han ministerial posts, restored the chancellorship, and filled it himself, concentrating supreme executive power.

sentences.zh: 孫吳、劉蜀，多依漢制，雖復臨時命氏，而無忝舊章。

translations.literal: Eastern Wu and Liu Bei's Shu largely followed Han institutions; though they sometimes improvised titles on the spot, they did not shame the old statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Wu and Shu largely kept Han models; occasional improvised titles notwithstanding, they stayed within the classical mold.

sentences.zh: 世祖武皇帝即位之初，以安平王孚為太宰，鄭沖為太傅，王祥為太保，司馬望為太尉，何曾為司徒，荀顗為司空，石苞為大司馬，陳騫為大將軍，世所謂八公同辰，攀雲附翼者也。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu the Shizu first ascended the throne, he appointed Prince Fu of Anping as Grand Preceptor, Zheng Chong as Grand Tutor, Wang Xiang as Grand Guardian, Sima Wang as Minister of War, He Zeng as Minister of Education, Xun Yi as Minister of Works, Shi Bao as Grand Marshal, and Chen Qian as Grand General—what the age called the eight dukes sharing one hour, climbing clouds and attaching wings.
translations.idiomatic: At his accession, Emperor Wu named Sima Fu Grand Preceptor, Zheng Chong Grand Tutor, Wang Xiang Grand Guardian, Sima Wang Minister of War, He Zeng Minister of Education, Xun Yi Minister of Works, Shi Bao Grand Marshal, and Chen Qian Grand General—the storied eight dukes of a single hour, men who rose by riding imperial favor.

sentences.zh: 若乃成乎棟宇，非一枝之勢；

translations.literal: As for completing roof-beams and rafters—it is not the strength of a single branch;
translations.idiomatic: Raising the whole hall takes more than one timber;

sentences.zh: 處乎經綸，稱萬夫之敵。

translations.literal: to dwell in ordering the realm is to be called a match for ten thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: true stewardship of the realm earns the title match for ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 或牽羊以葉於夢，或垂釣以申其道，或空桑以獻其術，或操版以啟其心。

translations.literal: Some led sheep and answered a leaf in a dream; some angled with a hook to proclaim their Way; some offered their arts from an empty mulberry; some grasped the tablet to open the ruler's mind.
translations.idiomatic: Some arrived through dreams of sheep and grain; some through fishing metaphors; some from humble soil with a craft to sell; some by presenting the royal tablet and winning trust.

sentences.zh: 臥龍飛鴻，方金擬璧，秦奚、鄭產，楚材晉用，斯亦曩時之良具，其又昭彰者焉。

translations.literal: The sleeping dragon, the soaring wild goose—square metal compared to round jade; the shepherd of Qin, the prodigy of Zheng; Chu talent employed by Jin—these too were fine instruments of former times, and no less manifest.
translations.idiomatic: Hidden dragons and soaring swans, talents weighed like gold against jade—think of Baili Xi, of Zichan's picks, or Chu officers serving Jin: the tools of antiquity for finding ministers were plain enough.

sentences.zh: 宣王既誅曹爽，政由己出，網羅英俊，以備天官。

translations.literal: Once Prince Xuan had executed Cao Shuang, government proceeded from himself alone; he gathered capable men to fill the celestial offices.
translations.idiomatic: After Sima Yi eliminated Cao Shuang, he ruled in his own name and stocked every court post with talent.

sentences.zh: 及蘭卿受羈，貴公顯戮，雖復策名魏氏，而乃心皇晉。

translations.literal: When worthy ministers were placed under restraint and eminent dukes suffered public execution—though they still bore registration under the Wei, their hearts were with the august Jin.
translations.idiomatic: When fine officers were seized and great nobles died in public execution, names might still stand with Wei but hearts had already turned to Jin.

sentences.zh: 及文王纂業，初啟晉台，始置二衛，有前驅養由之弩；

translations.literal: When King Wen continued the enterprise and first opened the Jin terrace, he began setting up the Two Guards, including front-vanguard crossbows like Yang Youji's.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Zhao extended the family work and founded the Jin apparatus, he created the Two Guards with vanguard crossbows worthy of Yang Youji.

sentences.zh: 及設三部，有熊渠佽飛之眾。

translations.literal: When the Three Departments were established, there were masses like the royal swimmers of Xiong Qu.
translations.idiomatic: When the Three Corps followed, they swelled with crack troops like the ancient palace guard.

sentences.zh: 是以武帝龍飛，乘茲奮翼，猶武王以周之十亂而理殷民者也。

translations.literal: Therefore when Emperor Wu ascended like a dragon, riding this to beat his wings, it was like King Wu of Zhou using the Zhou's ten ministers to govern the Yin people.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Emperor Wu's rise—vaulting on these preparations—matched King Wu deploying his ten able assistants to rule the former Shang subjects.

sentences.zh: 是以泰始盡于太康，喬柯茂葉，來居斯位；

translations.literal: Thus from Taishi through Taikang, tall trees with lush foliage came to occupy these posts;
translations.idiomatic: From the Taishi era through Taikang, imposing figures filled those ranks;

sentences.zh: 自太興訖於建元，南金北銑，用處茲秩。

translations.literal: from Daxing down to Jianyuan, southern gold and northern ore were employed in these ranks.
translations.idiomatic: from Daxing to Jianyuan, the finest metal south and north filled those offices.

sentences.zh: 雖未擬乎夔拊龍言，天工人代，亦庶幾乎任官惟賢，蒞事惟能者也。

translations.literal: Though they did not equal Kui's drumming and Long's pronouncements—Heaven's work and man's substitute—they approximated appoint officials only for worth, approach affairs only by ability.
translations.idiomatic: They fell short of the sage-kings' marriage of Heaven's work to human agency, yet they neared the ideal: office by virtue, tasks by competence.

sentences.zh: 丞相、相國，並秦官也。

translations.literal: Chancellor and minister of state were both Qin offices.
translations.idiomatic: The titles chancellor and minister of state both originated in Qin.

sentences.zh: 晉受魏禪，並不置，自惠帝之後，省置無恆。

translations.literal: When Jin received Wei's abdication, neither was established; from Emperor Hui onward, abolition and establishment were not constant.
translations.idiomatic: Jin left both vacant at the founding; after Emperor Hui the posts flickered in and out without a fixed rule.

sentences.zh: 為之者，趙王倫、梁王肜、成都王穎、南陽王保、王敦、王導之徒，皆非復尋常人臣之職。

translations.literal: Those who held them—Zhao Wang Lun, Liang Wang Rong, Chengdu Wang Ying, Nanyang Wang Bao, Wang Dun, Wang Dao, and the like—were no longer the duties of ordinary ministers.
translations.idiomatic: When princes such as Sima Lun, Sima Rong, Sima Ying, Sima Bao, Wang Dun, and Wang Dao took these titles, they wielded power far beyond an ordinary subject's charge.

sentences.zh: 太宰、太傅、太保，周之三公官也。

translations.literal: Grand Preceptor, Grand Tutor, and Grand Guardian were the Three Dukes of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Preceptor, Grand Tutor, and Grand Guardian were Zhou's classical Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 魏初唯置太傅，以鐘繇為之，末年又置太保，以鄭沖為之。

translations.literal: At the start of Wei only Grand Tutor was set up, with Zhong Yao holding it; toward the end Grand Guardian was added, with Zheng Chong holding it.
translations.idiomatic: Early Wei appointed only a Grand Tutor—Zhong Yao—and near the dynasty's end added a Grand Guardian, Zheng Chong.

sentences.zh: 晉初以景帝諱故，又采《周官》官名，置太宰以代太師之任，秩增三司，與太傅太保皆為上公，論道經邦，燮理陰陽，無其人則闕。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jin, because of the taboo on Emperor Jing's name, and adopting titles from the Offices of Zhou, Grand Preceptor was established in place of Grand Instructor; the rank was raised above the Three Departments; together with Grand Tutor and Grand Guardian they formed the upper dukes, discussing the Way and ordering the state, harmonizing yin and yang; if there was no suitable person the post stayed vacant.
translations.idiomatic: Early Jin avoided the taboo on Sima Shi's name and borrowed Zhou ritual titles: Grand Preceptor replaced Grand Instructor, ranked above the Three Departments alongside Grand Tutor and Grand Guardian as upper dukes who counseled on the Way and the realm and balanced yin and yang—and remained empty when no one qualified.

sentences.zh: 以安平獻王孚居之。

translations.literal: Prince Xian of Anping, Fu, occupied it.
translations.idiomatic: The office went to Sima Fu, Prince Xian of Anping.

sentences.zh: 自渡江以後，其名不替，而居之者甚寡。

translations.literal: After crossing the river the name was not dropped, but those who held it were very few.
translations.idiomatic: South of the Yangzi the title survived, yet almost nobody actually held it.

sentences.zh: 太尉、司徒、司空，並古官也。

translations.literal: Minister of War, Minister of Education, and Minister of Works are all ancient offices.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers of war, education, and works were ancient posts.

sentences.zh: 自漢曆魏，置以為三公。

translations.literal: From Han through Wei they were established as the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: Han and Wei treated them as the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 及晉受命，迄江左，其官相承不替。

translations.literal: When Jin received the mandate down to the Jiang left, these offices continued in unbroken succession.
translations.idiomatic: From Jin's founding through the southern court the succession never broke.

sentences.zh: 大司馬，古官也。

translations.literal: Grand Marshal is an ancient office.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Marshal was an ancient title.

sentences.zh: 漢制以冠大將軍、驃騎、車騎之上，以代太尉之職，故恆與太尉迭置，不並列。

translations.literal: Han regulations placed it above Grand General, Cavalry-in-Chief, and Chariots-in-Chief, substituting for the Minister of War; therefore it alternated with the Minister of War and was not held concurrently.
translations.idiomatic: Han ranked it above the chief generals as stand-in for Minister of War, so it rotated with that office rather than sitting beside it.

sentences.zh: 及魏有太尉，而大司馬、大將軍各自為官，位在三司上。

translations.literal: When Wei had a Minister of War, Grand Marshal and Grand General each became separate offices, ranking above the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wei the Minister of War returned as its own post while Grand Marshal and Grand General sat above the Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 晉受魏禪，因其制，以安平王孚為太宰，鄭沖為太傅。

translations.literal: When Jin received Wei's abdication, following that system, Prince Fu of Anping became Grand Preceptor and Zheng Chong Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Jin kept Wei's scheme: Sima Fu as Grand Preceptor, Zheng Chong as Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 王祥為太保，義陽王望為太尉，何曾為司徒，荀顗為司空，石苞為大司馬，陳騫為大將軍，凡八公同時並置，唯無丞相焉。

translations.literal: Wang Xiang as Grand Guardian, Prince Wang of Yiyang as Minister of War, He Zeng as Minister of Education, Xun Yi as Minister of Works, Shi Bao as Grand Marshal, Chen Qian as Grand General—in all eight dukes were established at once; only the chancellor was missing.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xiang became Grand Guardian, Sima Wang Minister of War, He Zeng Minister of Education, Xun Yi Minister of Works, Shi Bao Grand Marshal, Chen Qian Grand General—all eight peers at once, the chancellor alone omitted.

sentences.zh: 自義陽王望為大司馬之後，定令如舊，在三司上。

translations.literal: After Prince Wang of Yiyang became Grand Marshal, the fixed regulations were as before: it ranked above the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: After Sima Wang took Grand Marshal, statute fixed it as before—above the Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 開府儀同三司，漢官也。

translations.literal: Establishing a headquarters with ceremonies equal to the Three Departments is a Han office.
translations.idiomatic: The cluster full headquarters, ritual parity with the Three Departments was Han in origin.

sentences.zh: 殤帝延平元年，鄭騭為車騎將軍，儀同三司；

translations.literal: In the first year of Yanping of Emperor Shang, Zheng Zhi was chariots-and-cavalry general with ritual parity with the Three Departments;
translations.idiomatic: In 106 CE Emperor Shang named Zheng Zhi chariot-and-cavalry general with Three-Department ceremonial rank;

sentences.zh: 儀同之名，始自此也。

translations.literal: the name ritual parity begins from this.
translations.idiomatic: that is when ritual parity first appears.

sentences.zh: 及魏黃權以車騎將軍開府儀同三司；

translations.literal: When Wei made Huang Quan chariot-and-cavalry general who established headquarters with ritual parity with the Three Departments;
translations.idiomatic: Wei later gave Huang Quan chariot command, full headquarters, and Three-Department parity;

sentences.zh: 開府之名，起於此也。

translations.literal: the name establish headquarters arises from this.
translations.idiomatic: the establish headquarters formula dates from then.

sentences.zh: 驃騎、車騎、衛將軍、伏波、撫軍、都護、鎮軍、中軍、四征、四鎮、龍驤、典軍、上軍、輔國等大將軍，左右光祿、光祿三大夫，開府者皆為位從公。

translations.literal: Cavalry-in-Chief, chariots-in-Chief, guards general, wave-quelling, army-soothing, protector-in-Chief, garrison army, central army, Four Expeditions, Four Garrisons, soaring dragon, army directorate, upper army, state-supporting, and other grand generals; left and right splendid luminaries and the three splendid luminaries grandees—those who established headquarters all ranked as secondary to the dukes.
translations.idiomatic: Every stripe of grand general—the chief cavalry and chariot commands, palace guard, expeditionary and garrison posts, and the rest—plus senior Splendid Luminaries grandees: anyone who opened a mansion ranked just below full duke.

sentences.zh: 太宰、太傅、太保、司徒、司空、左右光祿大夫、光祿大夫，開府位從公者為文官公，冠進賢三梁，黑介幘。

translations.literal: Grand Preceptor, Grand Tutor, Grand Guardian, Ministers of Education and Works, left and right splendid luminaries grandees, splendid luminaries grandees—those who opened headquarters as secondary to dukes were civil dukes; they wore the three-rib advanced-worth cap with black scarf.
translations.idiomatic: Civil junior dukes—Grand Preceptor through Splendid Luminaries holders who ran full staffs—wore the three-ridged scholar cap and black kerchief.

sentences.zh: 大司馬、大將軍、太尉、驃騎、車騎、衛將軍、諸大將軍，開府位從公者為武官公，皆著武冠，平上黑幘。

translations.literal: Grand Marshal, Grand General, Minister of War, cavalry-in-Chief, chariots-in-Chief, guards general, various grand generals—those who opened headquarters as secondary to dukes were military dukes; all wore military caps with flat-top black scarves.
translations.idiomatic: Military junior dukes—the top martial posts with full headquarters—wore the warrior's cap and flat black scarf.

sentences.zh: 文武官公，皆假金章紫綬，著五時服。

translations.literal: Civil and military dukes all wore gold seals with purple ribbons and the five-seasons robes.
translations.idiomatic: Both kinds bore gold seals on purple cords and seasonal court dress.

sentences.zh: 其相國、丞相，皆袞冕，綠盭綬，所以殊于常公也。

translations.literal: Ministers of state and chancellors wore coronation robes and caps with green twisted ribbons—whereby they differed from ordinary dukes.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellors and ministers of state alone wore full ritual robes and green ribbons—marking them above ordinary peers.

sentences.zh: 諸公及開府位從公加兵者，增置司馬一人，秩千石；

translations.literal: For dukes and secondary dukes with headquarters who held military authority, one adjutant was added at rank one thousand shi;
translations.idiomatic: Junior dukes with troops added one adjutant at one thousand shi salary;

sentences.zh: 從事中郎二人，秩比千石；

translations.literal: two attendant gentlemen-inside at salary comparable to one thousand shi;
translations.idiomatic: two senior staff officers at near-thousand-shi pay;

sentences.zh: 主簿、記室督各一人；

translations.literal: one chief clerk and one secretary supervisor each;
translations.idiomatic: one chief clerk and one secretary supervisor;

sentences.zh: 舍人四人；

translations.literal: four gentlemen-attendants;
translations.idiomatic: four attendants;

sentences.zh: 兵鎧、士曹，營軍、刺奸、帳下都督，外都督，令史各一人。

translations.literal: one each for armor office, gentlemen office, camp army, inspector of malfeasance, household-area commander, external commander, and clerks.
translations.idiomatic: single posts for armor, personnel, camp affairs, discipline, household guard, external command, and records.

sentences.zh: 主簿已下，令史已上，皆絳服。

translations.literal: From chief clerk downward and clerk upward—all wore crimson robes.
translations.idiomatic: Staff from chief clerk through clerks wore crimson.

sentences.zh: 司馬給吏卒如長史，從事中郎給侍二人，主簿、記室督各給侍一人。

translations.literal: The adjutant was supplied clerks and runners like the chief clerk; each attendant gentleman-inside received two attendants; chief clerk and secretary supervisor each received one attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Adjutants received runners like chief clerks; attendant gentlemen got two pages; chief clerk and secretary one each.

sentences.zh: 其餘臨時增崇者，則褒加各因其時為節文，不為定制。

translations.literal: Other temporary elevations followed seasonal commendations as circumstances demanded; they were not fixed regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Ad hoc honors followed occasion and were never codified.

sentences.zh: 諸公及開府位從公為持節都督，增參車為六人，長史、司馬、從事中郎、主簿、記室督、祭酒、掾屬、舍人如常加兵公制。

translations.literal: When dukes and secondary dukes became credential-bearing area commanders, military advisers were increased to six; chief clerk, adjutant, attendant gentlemen, chief clerk, secretary supervisor, libationer, staff, and attendants followed the usual regulations for dukes with troops.
translations.idiomatic: Credential-bearing commanders among junior dukes carried six military advisers; other staff matched armed-duke precedent.

sentences.zh: 左右光祿大夫，假金章紫綬。

translations.literal: Left and right splendid luminaries grandees wore gold seals with purple ribbons.
translations.idiomatic: Senior Splendid Luminaries wore gold-and-purple insignia.

sentences.zh: 光祿大夫加金章紫綬者，品秩第二，祿賜、班位、冠幘、車服、佩玉，置吏卒羽林及卒，諸所賜給皆與特進同。

translations.literal: Splendid luminaries grandees granted gold seal and purple ribbon were grade two; stipends, seating, caps, carriages, robes, jade pendants, clerks, runners, feathered-forest guards—all grants matched extraordinary-advance status.
translations.idiomatic: Gold-purple Splendid Luminaries ranked second grade with stipends, precedence, dress, carriages, jade, and guards matching special advancement.

sentences.zh: 其以為加官者，唯假章綬、祿賜班位而已，不別給車服吏卒也。

translations.literal: Those who held it as supernumerary office received only seals, ribbons, stipends, and seating—not separate carriages, robes, clerks, or runners.
translations.idiomatic: Supernumerary appointees received only insignia and pay—not full perquisites.

sentences.zh: 又卒贈此位，本已有卿官者，不復重給吏卒，其餘皆給。

translations.literal: Moreover, posthumous grants to this rank: if the deceased already held minister rank, runners were not granted again; otherwise all were supplied.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumous awards skipped duplicate runners for men already at minister rank; others received full suites.

sentences.zh: 光祿大夫假銀章青綬者，品秩第三，位在金紫將軍下，諸卿上。

translations.literal: Splendid luminaries grandees with silver seal and blue ribbon were grade three, below gold-purple generals and above the various ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Silver-blue Splendid Luminaries ranked third—below gold-purple generals but above ordinary ministers.

sentences.zh: 漢時所置無定員，多以為拜假賵贈之使，及監護喪事。

translations.literal: In Han there was no fixed quota; they were often used as envoys for investitures, gifts, and funeral oversight.
translations.idiomatic: Han used them flexibly—often as ceremonial envoys or funeral supervisors.

sentences.zh: 魏氏已來，轉復優重，不復以為使命之官。

translations.literal: Since Wei they grew steadily weightier and ceased to be mere mission offices.
translations.idiomatic: After Wei they became honorific rather than errand posts.

sentences.zh: 其諸公告老者，皆家拜此位；

translations.literal: When various dukes retired, they were all appointed to this rank at home;
translations.idiomatic: Retiring dukes typically received this title by domestic edict;

sentences.zh: 及在朝顯職，復用加之，及晉受命，仍舊不改，復以為優崇之制。

translations.literal: and for prominent posts at court it was again conferred; when Jin received the mandate it continued unchanged, again treating it as a system of honor.
translations.idiomatic: Active ministers might earn it too; Jin kept the practice as a mark of esteem.

sentences.zh: 而諸公遜位，不復加之，或更拜上公，或以本封食公祿。

translations.literal: But when dukes yielded office they were not given it again; some were promoted to upper duke, some drew duke stipends from their original fiefs.
translations.idiomatic: Stepping-down dukes did not receive it again—some became upper dukes, others lived on fief income.

sentences.zh: 其諸卿尹中朝大官年老致仕者，及內外之職加此者，前後甚眾。

translations.literal: Among ministers and capital officials who retired for age, and inner and outer posts given this rank, there were very many over time.
translations.idiomatic: Many retired ministers and officials inside and outside received it.

sentences.zh: 由是或因得開府，或進加金章紫綬，又復以為禮贈之位。

translations.literal: Hence some thereby gained headquarters, some advanced to gold seal and purple ribbon; it also served as a courtesy gift rank.
translations.idiomatic: Some parlayed it into a headquarters appointment or gold-purple rank; it doubled as a ceremonial posthumous grade.

sentences.zh: 泰始中，唯太子詹事楊珧加給事中光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In Taishi only Yang Yao, supervisor of the heir apparent's household, was additionally appointed attendant-within and splendid luminaries grandee.
translations.idiomatic: During Taishi only Yang Yao combined household supervisor with attendant-within and Splendid Luminaries.

sentences.zh: 加兵之制，諸所供給依三品將軍。

translations.literal: For systems with added military authority, all provisions followed third-grade generals.
translations.idiomatic: Military add-ons followed third-rank general perquisites.

sentences.zh: 其餘自如舊制，終武、惠、孝懷三世。

translations.literal: The rest followed old regulations through the reigns of Wu, Hui, and Xiaohuai.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise old rules held through three reigns until collapse.

sentences.zh: 驃騎已下及諸大將軍不開府非持節都督者，品秩第二，其祿與特進同。

translations.literal: Cavalry-in-Chief downward and various grand generals who did not open headquarters and were not credential-bearing commanders were grade second; their stipends matched extraordinary advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Junior martial peers without mansions or credentials ranked second with stipends like special advancement.

sentences.zh: 置長史、司馬各一人，秩千石；

translations.literal: One chief clerk and one adjutant each at one thousand shi;
translations.idiomatic: Each carried chief clerk and adjutant at one thousand shi;

sentences.zh: 主簿，功曹史，門下督，錄事，兵鎧士賊曹，營軍、刺奸、帳下都督，功曹書佐門吏，門下書吏各一人。

translations.literal: chief clerk, merit clerk, household inspector, recorder, armor office, gentlemen-thieves office, camp army, malfeasance inspector, household-area commander, merit clerk clerk assistants, gate clerks—one each.
translations.idiomatic: full secretarial staff—chief clerk through gate clerks—one per slot.

sentences.zh: 其假節為都督者，所置與四征鎮加大將軍不開府為都督者同。

translations.literal: Those with borrowed credentials serving as commanders had the same staffing as expedition and garrison grand generals without headquarters serving as commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Credential-only commanders matched expeditionary grand generals without mansions.

sentences.zh: 四征鎮安平加大將軍不開府、持節都督者，品秩第二，置參佐吏卒，幕府兵騎如常都督制，唯朝會祿賜從二品將軍之例。

translations.literal: Four expeditions, garrisons, pacification, peace with added grand general title, without headquarters, credential-bearing commanders were grade second; staff and runners followed ordinary commander rules; only court assembly stipends followed second-grade general precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Expeditionary grand generals with credentials but no mansion ranked second; staffs matched normal commanders; court pay followed second-grade rules.

sentences.zh: 然則持節、都督無定員，前漢遣使始有持節。

translations.literal: Thus credential-bearing commanders had no fixed quota; Former Han first had credential-bearing envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Area commanders had no fixed headcount; Former Han invented credential-bearing missions.

sentences.zh: 光武建武初，征伐四方，始權時置督軍御史，事竟罷。

translations.literal: At the start of Guangwu's Jianwu, campaigning in four directions, temporary army-supervising censors were first set up; when the task ended they were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Guangwu's early campaigns used temporary army censors, then disbanded them.

sentences.zh: 建安中，魏武為相，始遣大將軍督之。

translations.literal: In Jian'an, Wei Wu as chancellor first dispatched grand generals to supervise.
translations.idiomatic: Mid-Jian'an Cao Cao as chancellor began assigning grand generals to oversee armies.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，征孫權還，夏侯惇督二十六軍是也。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, returning from campaigning against Sun Quan, Xiahou Dun supervised twenty-six armies—this is an instance.
translations.idiomatic: In 216 Xiahou Dun commanded twenty-six armies after the Wu campaign—a milestone.

sentences.zh: 魏文帝黃初三年，始置都督諸州軍事，或領刺史。

translations.literal: In Wei Wendi's third Huangchu year, commanders-in-chief of military affairs of various provinces were first established; some concurrently held inspector posts.
translations.idiomatic: 222 CE introduced provincial military commanders, often doubling as governors.

sentences.zh: 又上軍大將軍曹真都督中外諸軍事、假黃鉞，則總統內外諸軍矣。

translations.literal: Moreover Upper-army Grand General Cao Zhen commanded inner and outer armies with borrowed yellow axe—thus he commanded all armies within and without.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Zhen as senior grand general with the golden axe commanded every army at court and frontier.

sentences.zh: 魏明帝太和四年秋，宣帝征蜀，加號大都督。

translations.literal: Autumn of Wei Mingdi's fourth Taihe year, Prince Xuan campaigned against Shu and added the title supreme commander.
translations.idiomatic: 227 CE Sima Yi took the supreme commander title for the Shu expedition.

sentences.zh: 高貴鄉公正元二年，文帝都督中外諸軍，尋加大都督。

translations.literal: In Gaoguixiang Duke's second Zhenyuan year, Prince Wen commanded inner and outer armies; soon after he added supreme commander.
translations.idiomatic: 254 CE Sima Zhao commanded all forces, then took supreme commander.

sentences.zh: 及晉受禪，都督諸軍為上，臨諸軍次之，督諸軍為下；

translations.literal: When Jin received abdication, commander-in-chief of various armies was highest, overseeing various armies next, supervising various armies lowest;
translations.idiomatic: Jin ranked titles: commander-in-chief highest, overseer next, supervisor lowest;

sentences.zh: 使持節為上，持節次之，假節為下。

translations.literal: Bearer of full powers highest, credential-holder next, borrowed credential lowest.
translations.idiomatic: Full powers ranked above ordinary credential, which ranked above borrowed.

sentences.zh: 使持節得殺二千石以下；

translations.literal: Bearer of full powers could execute officials down to two thousand shi;
translations.idiomatic: Full powers allowed executing officials through two-thousand-shi rank;

sentences.zh: 持節殺無官位人，若軍事，得與使持節同；

translations.literal: credential-holder could kill persons without office rank; in military matters could match bearer of full powers;
translations.idiomatic: Ordinary credentials covered commoners; in war matched full powers;

sentences.zh: 假節唯軍事得殺犯軍令者。

translations.literal: borrowed credential only in military affairs could kill violators of military orders.
translations.idiomatic: Borrowed credentials executed only military offenders.

sentences.zh: 江左以來，都督中外尤重，唯王導等權重者乃居之。

translations.literal: Since the Jiang left, commander-in-chief of inner and outer has been especially weighty; only men of heavy authority like Wang Dao have held it.
translations.idiomatic: South of the river, supreme command rarely fell except to figures as powerful as Wang Dao.

sentences.zh: 三品將軍秩中二千石者，著武冠，平上黑幘，五時朝服，佩水蒼玉，食奉、春秋賜綿絹、菜田、田騶如光祿大夫諸卿制。

translations.literal: Third-grade generals at salary two thousand shi wore military caps, flat-top black scarves, five-seasons court robes, dark aquamarine jade; salary, spring-autumn silk grants, vegetable fields, field runners matched splendid luminaries grandees and various ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Third-grade two-thousand-shi generals wore warrior dress and seasonal court robes with dark jade; pay and land grants matched ministers.

sentences.zh: 置長史、司馬各一人，秩千石；

translations.literal: One chief clerk and one adjutant each at one thousand shi;
translations.idiomatic: Staff included chief clerk and adjutant at one thousand shi;

sentences.zh: 主簿，功曹，門下都督，錄事，兵鎧士賊曹，營軍、刺奸吏、帳下都督，功曹書佐門吏，門下書吏各一人。

translations.literal: chief clerk, merit clerk, household commander, recorder, armor office, gentlemen-thieves office, camp army, malfeasance clerk, household-area commander, merit clerk assistants, gate clerks, household clerks—one each.
translations.idiomatic: plus the full clerical roster—chief clerk through household clerks—one per position.

sentences.zh: 尚書令，秩千石，假銅印墨綬，冠進賢兩梁冠，納言幘，五時朝服，佩水蒼玉，食奉月五十斛。

translations.literal: The Director of the Secretariat had salary rank one thousand shi, borrowed bronze seal with black ribbon, wore the two-beam advanced-worth cap and speaking-inner scarf, five-seasons court dress, dark aquamarine jade at the belt, and a monthly grain allowance of fifty hu.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat director drew one thousand shi, bearing a bronze seal on a black ribbon; he wore the two-ridged scholar cap and inner-court kerchief, seasonal court robes, dark jade, and fifty hu of grain each month.

sentences.zh: 受拜則策命之，以在端右故也。

translations.literal: Upon investiture he received a written edict of appointment, because he stood at the right head of the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Investiture came by formal edict—his seat was the premier place at the hall's right.

sentences.zh: 太康二年，始給賜絹，春三十匹，秋七十匹。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taikang they began granting silk—thirty bolts in spring and seventy in autumn.
translations.idiomatic: From 281 onward the court added silk grants—thirty bolts each spring and seventy each autumn.

sentences.zh: 綿七十斤。

translations.literal: Seventy jin of cotton.
translations.idiomatic: They also issued seventy jin of cotton.

sentences.zh: 元康元年，始給菜田六頃，田騶六人，立夏後不及田者，食奉一年。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuankang they began granting six qing of vegetable land and six field runners; if after the beginning of summer the land had still not been awarded, he received one year's salary instead.
translations.idiomatic: From 291 vegetable plots of six qing plus six field runners applied; if fields were not assigned after summer began, the stipend was paid in cash for a full year.

sentences.zh: 始賈充為尚書令，以目疾表置省事吏四人，省事蓋自此始。

translations.literal: When Jia Chong first became Director of the Secretariat, because of eye trouble he memorialized to appoint four clerks for miscellaneous duties—the office of miscellaneous-affairs clerk probably began here.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Chong, first as director, secured four auxiliary clerks for routine paperwork—likely the origin of the 'miscellaneous clerk' post.

sentences.zh: 僕射，服秩印綬與令同。

translations.literal: The vice directors had the same robes, rank, seal, and ribbon as the director.
translations.idiomatic: Vice directors matched the director in dress, grade, seal, and ribbon.

sentences.zh: 案漢本置一人，至漢獻帝建安四年，以執金吾榮郃為尚書左僕射，僕射分置左右，蓋自此始。

translations.literal: Originally Han established only one person; in the fourth year of Jian'an under Emperor Xian, the superintendent of the guards Rong He was made Left Vice Director of the Secretariat—the division into left and right vice directors began here.
translations.idiomatic: Han began with a single vice director; in 199 Rong He of the imperial guards became the first left vice director—splitting the post into left and right starts there.

sentences.zh: 經魏至晉，迄于江左，省置無恆，置二，則為左右僕射，或不兩置，但曰尚書僕射。

translations.literal: From Wei through Jin down to the southern court, abolition and restoration were irregular; when two were set they were left and right vice directors; when both were not filled the title was simply Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Wei and Jin kept reshuffling the posts south of the river: two seats meant left and right; a lone officer was just 'Vice Director.'

sentences.zh: 令闕，則左為省主；

translations.literal: When the director was vacant, the left vice director served as head of the department;
translations.idiomatic: If the director's chair was empty, the left vice director ran the office;

sentences.zh: 若左右並闕，則置尚書僕射以主左事。

translations.literal: if both left and right were vacant, a Vice Director of the Secretariat was appointed to oversee left-side affairs.
translations.idiomatic: when both vice seats were empty, a single vice director stepped in to manage the left bench.

sentences.zh: 列曹尚書，案尚書本漢承秦置，及武帝遊宴後庭，始用宦者主中書，以司馬遷為之，中間遂罷其官，以為中書之職。

translations.literal: The various bureau Masters of Writing—in origin the Secretariat continued Qin under Han; when Emperor Wu feasted in the inner palace he first used eunuchs to manage the Palace Secretariat and appointed Sima Qian to it; in the middle period that office was abolished and its duties were folded into the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The bureau system grew from Qin and Han: Emperor Wu had eunuchs run palace drafting with Sima Qian nominally attached; later that office was folded into what became the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 至成帝建始四年，罷中書宦者，又置尚書五人，一人為僕射，而四人分為四曹，通掌圖書秘記章奏之事，各有其任。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jiushi under Chengdi the Zhongshu eunuchs were abolished and five Masters of Writing were again appointed—one serving as vice director and four forming four bureaus jointly handling archives, secret records, and memorials, each with its charge.
translations.idiomatic: In 29 BCE Chengdi dismissed the eunuch secretariat and set five Masters of Writing—one vice director plus four bureaus sharing libraries, classified documents, and memorial traffic.

sentences.zh: 其一曰常侍曹，主丞相御史公卿事。

translations.literal: The first was called the Permanent Attendant Bureau—it handled the chancellor, the censorate, and the ranks of ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The first desk was the Permanent Attendant Bureau—for the chancellor, censorate, and senior ministers.

sentences.zh: 其二曰二千石曹，主刺史郡國事。

translations.literal: The second was called the Two-Thousand-Shi Bureau—it handled inspectors and commandery-kingdom affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The second was the two-thousand-shi desk—for regional inspectors and local administration.

sentences.zh: 其三曰民曹，主吏民上書事。

translations.literal: The third was called the People Bureau—it handled clerks and commoners submitting memorials.
translations.idiomatic: The third covered popular petitions—clerks and lay memorials.

sentences.zh: 其四曰主客曹，主外國夷狄事。

translations.literal: The fourth was called the Host-Guest Bureau—it handled foreign tribes and barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: The fourth handled foreigners—tribute missions and border peoples.

sentences.zh: 後成帝又置三公曹，主斷獄，是為五曹。

translations.literal: Later Chengdi also established the Three Dukes Bureau to decide criminal cases—thus there were five bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: Chengdi added a Three Dukes bench for trials, bringing the count to five.

sentences.zh: 後漢光武以三公曹主歲盡考課諸州郡事，改常侍曹為吏部曹，主選舉祠祀事，民曹主繕修功作鹽池園苑事，客曹主護駕羌胡朝賀事，二千石曹主辭訟事，中都官曹主水火盜賊事，合為六曹。

translations.literal: Later Han Emperor Guangwu used the Three Dukes Bureau for year-end assessment of commanderies and kingdoms; changed Permanent Attendant Bureau to Personnel Bureau for selections and sacrifices; People Bureau for repairs, projects, salt pools, and parks; Host-Guest Bureau for escorting the imperial carriage and Qiang-Hu court audiences; Two-Thousand-Shi Bureau for lawsuits; Capital Officials Bureau for fire, flood, theft, and banditry—together six bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: Guangwu repurposed the benches: year-end ratings moved to the Three Dukes desk; selections and rites went to Personnel; public works and fiscal estates to People; imperial progresses and barbarian audiences to Host-Guest; litigation to Two-Thousand-Shi; emergencies to Capital Officials—six lines in all.

sentences.zh: 並令僕二人，謂之八座。

translations.literal: Together with two vice directors they were called the Eight Seats.
translations.idiomatic: With two vice directors they formed the famed Eight Seats.

sentences.zh: 尚書雖有曹名，不以為號。

translations.literal: Although Masters of Writing had bureau names, those names were not yet formal titles.
translations.idiomatic: Bureaus had nicknames, but ministers were not yet titled after them.

sentences.zh: 靈帝以侍中梁鵠為選部尚書，于此始見曹名。

translations.literal: Emperor Ling appointed attendant Liang Hu as Minister of the Selection Bureau—here a bureau name first appeared in an official title.
translations.idiomatic: Lingdi's appointment of Liang Hu as 'Selection Bureau minister' was the first titled bureau post.

sentences.zh: 及魏改選部為吏部，主選部事，又有左民、客曹、五兵、度支、凡五曹尚書、二僕射、一令為八座。

translations.literal: Wei changed Selection Bureau to Personnel Bureau for selection affairs; there were also Left People, Host-Guest, Five Armies, and Fiscal Control—in all five bureau ministers, two vice directors, and one director making the Eight Seats.
translations.idiomatic: Wei renamed Selection to Personnel; People, Rites, Five Armies, and Fiscal joined—five ministers plus two vice directors and the director filled the Eight Seats.

sentences.zh: 及晉置吏部、三公、客曹、駕部、屯田、度支六曹、而無五兵。

translations.literal: When Jin set up Personnel, Three Dukes, Host-Guest, Chariots, Colony Fields, and Fiscal Control—six bureaus—there was no Five Armies bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Jin ran six desks—Personnel, Three Dukes, Host-Guest, Chariots, Colony Fields, Fiscal—and dropped Five Armies.

sentences.zh: 咸寧二年，省駕部尚書。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianning the Chariots Minister was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: 276 CE struck the chariot ministry.

sentences.zh: 四年，省一僕射，又置駕部尚書。

translations.literal: In the fourth year one vice director was cut, and the Chariots Minister was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later they trimmed a vice seat and brought chariots back.

sentences.zh: 太康中，有吏部、殿中及五兵、田曹、度支、左民為六曹尚書，又無駕部、三公、客曹。

translations.literal: During Taikang there were Personnel, Palace Hall, Five Armies, Fields Bureau, Fiscal Control, and Left People as six bureau ministers—again without Chariots, Three Dukes, or Host-Guest.
translations.idiomatic: Around Taikang the roster was Personnel, Palace Hall, Five Armies, Fields, Fiscal, and Left People—no chariot, Three Dukes, or guest desks.

sentences.zh: 惠帝世又有右民尚書，止于六曹，不知此時省何曹也。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Hui a Right People Minister appeared; there were still six bureaus—which bureau was dropped then is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Huidi added Right People while staying at six desks—which office vanished is unclear.

sentences.zh: 及渡江，有吏部、祠部、五兵、左民、度支五尚書。

translations.literal: After crossing the Yangzi there were Personnel, Sacrifices, Five Armies, Left People, and Fiscal Control—five ministers.
translations.idiomatic: South of the river the bench shrank to Personnel, Sacrifices, Five Armies, Left People, and Fiscal.

sentences.zh: 祠部尚書常與右僕射通職，不恆置，以右僕射攝之，若右僕射闕，則以祠部尚書攝知右事。

translations.literal: The Sacrifices Minister often rotated duty with the Right Vice Director—not permanently established; the Right Vice Director deputized; if the Right Vice Director was vacant the Sacrifices Minister acted for right-side affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifices paired with the right vice seat; if that seat sat empty, the Sacrifices minister covered right-bench business.

sentences.zh: 左右丞，自漢武帝建始四年置尚書，而便置丞四人。

translations.literal: The left and right assistants—since Emperor Wu established the Secretariat in the fourth year of Jian'shi, four assistants were immediately placed.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu founded the Secretariat in 29 BCE he attached four assistant commissioners.

sentences.zh: 及光武始減其二，唯置左右丞，左右丞蓋自此始也。

translations.literal: When Guangwu reduced them to two, only left and right assistants remained—the left and right assistants began here.
translations.idiomatic: Guangwu cut the four to the familiar left and right assistants.

sentences.zh: 自此至晉不改。

translations.literal: From then through Jin it was unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Jin kept that pairing intact.

sentences.zh: 晉左丞主台內禁令，宗廟祠祀，朝儀禮制，選用署吏，急假；

translations.literal: Under Jin the left assistant supervised inner prohibitions of the terrace, ancestral temple sacrifices, court etiquette and ritual codes, selection and appointment of clerks, and emergency leave;
translations.idiomatic: The left wing handled bans inside the tower, temple rites, protocol, clerk appointments, and leave requests;

sentences.zh: 右丞掌台內庫藏廬舍，凡諸器用之物，及廩振人租布，刑獄兵器，督錄遠道文書章表奏事。

translations.literal: the right assistant managed terrace treasuries and buildings, all sorts of equipment and goods, grain relief and rent cloth collections, criminal cases and weapons, and supervising transmission of distant memorials, petitions, and memorialized business.
translations.idiomatic: the right wing ran storerooms and buildings, supplies, rent cloth, prisons and arms, and long-distance paperwork.

sentences.zh: 八座郎初拜，皆沿漢舊制，並集都座交禮，遷職又解交焉。

translations.literal: When gentlemen of the Eight Seats were first invested they followed Han precedent: all gathered at the central dais to exchange bows; on promotion they again released the exchange bows.
translations.idiomatic: New Eight Seats still exchanged bows on the central dais per Han ritual and repeated the ceremony on transfer.

sentences.zh: 尚書郎，西漢舊置四人，以分掌尚書。

translations.literal: Gentlemen of the Secretariat—Western Han originally set four to divide supervision of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Han began with four Secretariat gentlemen splitting the workload.

sentences.zh: 其一人主匈奴單于營部，一人主羌夷吏民，一人主戶口墾田，一人主財帛委輸。

translations.literal: One supervised the Xiongnu shanyu's camp office, one supervised Qiang and Yi clerks and people, one supervised household registers and reclamation, one supervised wealth, silk, and transport.
translations.idiomatic: One tracked the Xiongnu court, one frontier tribes, one household and land registers, one revenue and logistics.

sentences.zh: 及光武分尚書為六曹之後，合置三十四人，秩四百石，並左右丞為三十六人。

translations.literal: After Guangwu divided the Secretariat into six bureaus, thirty-four were appointed together at salary four hundred shi; with left and right assistants they numbered thirty-six.
translations.idiomatic: Guangwu's six-bureau reform raised thirty-four gentlemen at four hundred shi, thirty-six with the assistants.

sentences.zh: 郎主作文書起草，更直五日於建禮門內。

translations.literal: The gentlemen drafted documents and rotated night duty five-day shifts inside the Jianli Gate.
translations.idiomatic: They drafted paperwork on five-day rotations inside Jianli Gate.

sentences.zh: 尚書郎初從三署詣台試，守尚書郎，中歲滿稱尚書郎，三年稱侍郎，選有吏能者為之。

translations.literal: Gentlemen of the Secretariat first came from the Three Offices to the terrace on probation as acting gentlemen; after one year within they were called Gentlemen of the Secretariat; after three years they were called deputy gentlemen; men of administrative talent were selected.
translations.idiomatic: Trainees arrived from the Three Offices, served probation, earned full gentleman status after a year and deputy rank after three—only capable men advanced.

sentences.zh: 至魏，尚書郎有殿中、吏部、駕部、金部、虞曹、比部、南主客、祠部、度支、庫部、農部、水部、儀曹、三公、倉部、民曹、二千石、中兵、外兵、都兵、別兵、考功、定課，凡二十三郎。

translations.literal: By Wei, gentlemen of the Secretariat included Palace Hall, Personnel, Chariots, Metals, Yu Bureau, Comparison Bureau, Southern Host-Guest, Sacrifices, Fiscal Control, Storehouse, Agriculture, Water, Rituals Bureau, Three Dukes, Granary, People, Two-Thousand-Shi, Central Army, Outer Army, Capital Army, Separate Army, Merit Assessment, Fixed Assessment—in all twenty-three gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Wei listed twenty-three specialty desks—from palace business through armies and budgets.

sentences.zh: 青龍二年，尚書陳矯奏置都官、騎兵，合凡二十五郎。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qinglong Minister Chen Jiao memorialized to add Capital Officials and Cavalry—twenty-five gentlemen altogether.
translations.idiomatic: 234 CE added Capital Officials and Cavalry bureaus for twenty-five lines.

sentences.zh: 每一郎缺，白試諸孝廉能結文案者五人，謹封奏其姓名以補之。

translations.literal: Whenever a gentleman post opened, they tested several recommended filial-and-incorrupt candidates who could compose documents; sealed memorials listed names for appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Vacancies drew sealed lists of recommended Filial-and-Incorrupt candidates who could draft.

sentences.zh: 及晉受命，武帝罷農部、定課，置直事、殿中、祠部、儀曹、吏部、三公、比部、金部、倉部、度支、都官、二千石、左民、右民、虞曹、屯田、起部、水部、左右主客、駕部、車部、庫部、左右中兵、左右外兵、別兵、都兵、騎兵、左右士、北主客、南主客，為三十四曹郎。

translations.literal: When Jin succeeded, Emperor Wu abolished Agriculture and Fixed Assessment, added duty affairs, Palace Hall, Sacrifices, Rituals, Personnel, Three Dukes, Comparison, Metals, Granary, Fiscal Control, Capital Officials, Two-Thousand-Shi, Left People, Right People, Yu Bureau, Colony Fields, Works, Water, Left and Right Host-Guest, Chariots, Coach Bureau, Storehouse, Left and Right Central Army, Left and Right Outer Army, Separate Army, Capital Army, Cavalry, Left and Right Gentlemen, Northern Host-Guest, Southern Host-Guest—thirty-four bureau gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's roster ballooned to thirty-four specialty desks—everything from duty rounds to north-south guest affairs.

sentences.zh: 後又置運曹，凡三十五曹，置郎二十三人，更相統攝。

translations.literal: Later Transport Bureau was added—thirty-five bureaus in all—twenty-three gentlemen appointed, overseeing one another.
translations.idiomatic: They later added Transport—thirty-five desks staffed by twenty-three gentlemen with overlapping duties.

sentences.zh: 及江左，無直事、右民、屯田、車部、別兵、都兵、騎兵、左右士、運曹十曹郎。

translations.literal: East of the Yangzi there were no Duty Affairs, Right People, Colony Fields, Coach Bureau, Separate Army, Capital Army, Cavalry, Left and Right Gentlemen, or Transport—ten bureau gentlemen cut.
translations.idiomatic: South of the river ten desks vanished—including transport and several army offices.

sentences.zh: 康穆以後，又無虞曹、二千石二郎，但有殿中、祠部、吏部、儀曹、三公、比部、金部、倉部、度支、都官、左民、起部、水部、主客、駕部、庫部、中兵、外兵十八曹郎。

translations.literal: After the Kang and Mu reigns Yu Bureau and Two-Thousand-Shi gentlemen were also gone; only Palace Hall, Sacrifices, Personnel, Rituals, Three Dukes, Comparison, Metals, Granary, Fiscal Control, Capital Officials, Left People, Works, Water, Host-Guest, Chariots, Storehouse, Central Army, Outer Army—eighteen bureau gentlemen remained.
translations.idiomatic: After Mid-Jin only eighteen desks survived—core fiscal, ritual, and military lines.

sentences.zh: 後又省主客、起部、水部，余十五曹雲。

translations.literal: Later Host-Guest, Works, and Water were also cut—fifteen bureaus remained.
translations.idiomatic: Three more desks—guest affairs, works, water—soon disappeared, leaving fifteen.

sentences.zh: 侍中，案黃帝時風後為侍中，于周為常伯之任，秦取古名置侍中，漢因之。

translations.literal: Palace attendant—in tradition Feng Hou under the Yellow Emperor was palace attendant; under Zhou it matched the permanent steward's duty; Qin borrowed the ancient name to establish palace attendant; Han continued it.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants traced to Feng Hou; Zhou called similar posts permanent stewards; Qin revived the title and Han kept it.

sentences.zh: 秦漢俱無定員，以功高者一人為僕射。

translations.literal: Qin and Han both had no fixed quota; the highest merit holder served as chief steward.
translations.idiomatic: Neither dynasty capped numbers; the senior man headed them as steward.

sentences.zh: 魏晉以來置四人，別加官者則非數。

translations.literal: Since Wei and Jin four were established; supernumerary appointees did not count toward the quota.
translations.idiomatic: Wei and Jin fixed four seats; extras sat outside the quota.

sentences.zh: 掌儐贊威儀，大駕出則次直侍中護駕，正直侍中負璽陪乘，不帶劍，餘皆騎從。

translations.literal: They conducted ceremonies and guarded imperial dignity; on great progresses the rotated attendant on duty guarded the carriage while the upright attendant carried the seal and rode pillion without sword; the rest rode escort.
translations.idiomatic: They staged ritual and guarded spectacles: rotated duty shielded the train; the 'upright' attendant carried the seal pillion without sword; others rode escort.

sentences.zh: 禦登殿，與散騎常侍對扶，侍中居左，常侍居右。

translations.literal: When the emperor mounted the hall they paired with elite cavalry standing attendants to assist—the attendant stood left, the standing attendant right.
translations.idiomatic: At imperial audiences they flanked the emperor with household standing attendants—attendant left, standing attendant right.

sentences.zh: 備切問近對，拾遺補闕。

translations.literal: They stood ready for intimate questions and nearby replies, gathering oversights and patching omissions.
translations.idiomatic: They answered spur-of-the-moment questions and caught policy gaps.

sentences.zh: 及江左哀帝興寧四年，桓溫奏省二人，後復舊。

translations.literal: East of the Yangzi, in the fourth year of Xing'ning under Emperor Ai, Huan Wen memorialized to remove two persons; later the old quota returned.
translations.idiomatic: In 366 Huan Wen briefly cut two seats; the full four returned afterward.

sentences.zh: 給事黃門侍郎，秦官也。

translations.literal: Gentleman attendant at the Yellow Gates—it was a Qin office.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow-gate attendant was a Qin title.

sentences.zh: 漢已後並因之，與侍中俱管門下眾事，無員。

translations.literal: After Han it continued; together with palace attendants they managed all gate-affairs business under no fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: Han onward paired them with palace attendants for gate business without a headcount cap.

sentences.zh: 及晉，置員四人。

translations.literal: Under Jin four posts were established.
translations.idiomatic: Jin capped the corps at four.

sentences.zh: 散騎常侍，本秦官也。

translations.literal: Elite cavalry standing attendant—it was originally a Qin office.
translations.idiomatic: Elite cavalry standing attendant began under Qin.

sentences.zh: 秦置散騎，又置中常侍，散騎騎從乘輿車後，中常侍得入禁中，皆無員，亦以為加官。

translations.literal: Qin established unattached cavalry and also palace standing attendants; unattached cavalry rode behind the imperial carriage; palace standing attendants could enter the forbidden quarters—both had no quota and served as supernumerary titles.
translations.idiomatic: Qin ran freelance riders behind the coach and inner-chamber standing attendants—both honorific and uncapped.

sentences.zh: 漢東京初，省散騎，而中常侍用宦者。

translations.literal: Early Eastern Han cut unattached cavalry and palace standing attendants used eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: Later Han dropped freelance riders and staffed standing attendants with eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 魏文帝黃初初，置散騎，合之於中常侍，同掌規諫，不典事，貂榼插右，騎而散從，至晉不改。

translations.literal: Wei Wendi at the start of Huangchu restored unattached cavalry, merged them with palace standing attendants to jointly offer counsel without managing affairs; marten-fur bags tucked right, riding loosely escorting—unchanged through Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Wei fused freelance riders with standing attendants as feather-light counselors—fur pouch on the right, mounted escort—and Jin kept the mold.

sentences.zh: 及元康中，惠帝始以宦者董猛為中常侍，後遂止。

translations.literal: In Yuankang under Emperor Hui the eunuch Dong Meng first became palace standing attendant; afterward it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: 296 CE briefly saw the eunuch Dong Meng as standing attendant—then the experiment ended.

sentences.zh: 常為顯職。

translations.literal: It was normally an eminent post.
translations.idiomatic: The post stayed an honor reserved for heavyweights.

sentences.zh: 給事中，秦官也。

translations.literal: Attendant-within—it was a Qin office.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant-within was another Qin survival.

sentences.zh: 所加或大夫、博士、議郎，掌顧問應對，位次中常侍。

translations.literal: Supernumerary holders might be grandees, erudites, or deliberation gentlemen; they handled consultation and replies, ranking below palace standing attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Added to ministers or scholars, they answered imperial queries—below standing attendants in rank.

sentences.zh: 漢因之。

translations.literal: Han continued it.
translations.idiomatic: Han kept the arrangement.

sentences.zh: 及漢東京省，魏世復置，至晉不改。

translations.literal: Eastern Han cut it; Wei restored it; unchanged through Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Later Han dropped it; Wei brought it back; Jin left it alone.

sentences.zh: 在散騎常侍下，給事黃門侍郎上，無員。

translations.literal: It ranked below elite cavalry standing attendant and above gentleman attendant at the Yellow Gates; no fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: It sat between standing attendants and Yellow Gates—again no fixed headcount.

sentences.zh: 通直散騎常侍，案魏末散騎常侍又有在員外者。

translations.literal: General-access elite cavalry standing attendant—under late Wei some elite cavalry standing attendants were outside the quota.
translations.idiomatic: Late Wei added general-access seats outside the regular standing-attendant quota.

sentences.zh: 泰始十年，武帝使二人與散騎常侍通員直，故謂之通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Taishi Emperor Wu made two men rotate duty jointly with elite cavalry standing attendants—therefore they were called general-access elite cavalry standing attendants.
translations.idiomatic: 274 CE paired two officers with standing attendants on shared rotations—hence 'general-access.'

sentences.zh: 江左置四人。

translations.literal: East of the Yangzi four were established.
translations.idiomatic: The southern court assigned four such posts.

sentences.zh: 員外散騎常侍，魏末置，無員。

translations.literal: Supernumerary elite cavalry standing attendant—established at end of Wei; no quota.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's end introduced supernumerary standing attendants outside the roster.

sentences.zh: 散騎侍郎四人，魏初與散騎常侍同置。

translations.literal: Four elite cavalry deputy gentlemen—Wei at the outset established them together with elite cavalry standing attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Wei founded four deputy gentlemen alongside standing attendants.

sentences.zh: 自魏至晉，散騎常侍、侍郎與侍中、黃門侍郎共平尚書奏事，江左乃罷。

translations.literal: From Wei through Jin, elite cavalry standing attendants and deputy gentlemen together with palace attendants and Yellow Gate gentlemen jointly adjudicated Secretariat memorials; east of the Yangzi this was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Wei-Jin let those officers vet Secretariat paperwork with attendants and Yellow Gates; the southern court ended that joint duty.

sentences.zh: 通直散騎侍郎四人。

translations.literal: Four general-access elite cavalry deputy gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Four general-access deputy gentlemen mirrored the standing-attendant rule.

sentences.zh: 初，武帝置員外散騎侍郎，及太興元年，元帝使二人與散騎侍郎通員直，故謂之通直散騎侍郎，後增為四人。

translations.literal: Originally Emperor Wu established supernumerary elite cavalry deputy gentlemen; in the first year of Taixing Emperor Yuan made two men rotate jointly with elite cavalry deputy gentlemen—therefore they were called general-access elite cavalry deputy gentlemen; later increased to four.
translations.idiomatic: Wu invented supernumerary deputies; 318 CE Yuan rotated two with regular deputies—'general-access' deputies—and later raised them to four.

sentences.zh: 員外散騎侍郎，武帝置，無員。

translations.literal: Supernumerary elite cavalry deputy gentlemen—Emperor Wu established them; no quota.
translations.idiomatic: Supernumerary deputies remained honorific extras without quota.

sentences.zh: 奉朝請，本不為官，無員。

translations.literal: Court-attending audience was originally not an office; there was no quota.
translations.idiomatic: 'Court attendance' was not a bureau and had no roster.

sentences.zh: 漢東京罷三公、外戚、宗室、諸侯多奉朝請。

translations.literal: Eastern Han abolished the Three Dukes; many imperial in-laws, imperial clansmen, and nobles held court-attending status.
translations.idiomatic: Later Han cashiered the Three Dukes and packed the audience rolls with kin and nobles.

sentences.zh: 奉朝請者，奉朝會請召而已。

translations.literal: Those who court-attended merely attended court assemblies and answered summons.
translations.idiomatic: It meant simply joining audiences when summoned.

sentences.zh: 武帝亦以宗室、外戚為奉車、駙馬、騎三都尉而奉朝請焉。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu also made imperial clansmen and in-laws chariot commandants, chief groom commandants, and cavalry commandants with court-attending status.
translations.idiomatic: Wudi likewise titled kin as chariot, chief groom, and cavalry commandants with audience privileges.

sentences.zh: 元帝為晉王，以參軍為奉車都尉，掾屬為駙馬都尉，行參軍舍人為騎都尉，皆奉朝請。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yuan was Prince of Jin he made adjutants chariot commandants, staff members chief groom commandants, and acting adjutants and attendants cavalry commandants—all court-attending.
translations.idiomatic: As Prince of Jin, Yuan titled adjutants chariot commandants, staff chief groom commandants, and acting staff as cavalry commandants—all court-attending.

sentences.zh: 後罷奉車、騎二都尉，唯留駙馬都尉奉朝請。

translations.literal: Later chariot and cavalry commandants were abolished; only chief groom commandants retained court-attending status.
translations.idiomatic: They later dropped chariot and cavalry commandants, leaving chief groom commandants with audience rights.

sentences.zh: 諸尚公主者劉惔、桓溫皆為之。

translations.literal: Those who married princesses—Liu Tan and Huan Wen both held it.
translations.idiomatic: Princess husbands such as Liu Tan and Huan Wen held that nominal duty.

sentences.zh: 中書監及令，案漢武帝游宴後庭，始使宦者典事尚書，謂之中書謁者，置令、僕射。

translations.literal: Palace Secretariat supervisor and director—in tradition Han Emperor Wu feasting in the inner palace first used eunuchs to manage Secretariat affairs, called Palace Secretariat visitors; director and vice director were set.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu's revels spawned eunuch-run palace drafting—styled Secretariat visitors—with director and deputy.

sentences.zh: 成帝改中書謁者令曰中謁者令，罷僕射。

translations.literal: Chengdi changed Palace Secretariat visitor director to inner visitor director and abolished the vice director.
translations.idiomatic: Chengdi renamed the visitor director and removed the deputy.

sentences.zh: 漢東京省中謁者令，而有中官謁者令，非其職也。

translations.literal: Eastern Han abolished inner visitor director but had inner-court visitor directors—not the same duty.
translations.idiomatic: Later Han dropped the inner title but kept eunuch visitors—a different job.

sentences.zh: 魏武帝為魏王，置秘書令，典尚書奏事。

translations.literal: Wei Emperor Wu as Prince of Wei established Secretary Director to handle Secretariat memorial business.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao as Wei prince created a secretary director for memorial traffic.

sentences.zh: 文帝黃初初改為中書，置監、令，以秘書左丞劉放為中書監，右丞孫資為中書令；

translations.literal: Wendi at the start of Huangchu changed it to Palace Secretariat, establishing supervisor and director—Secretariat left assistant Liu Fang became supervisor, right assistant Sun Zi became director;
translations.idiomatic: 220 CE rebranded the office: Liu Fang supervised, Sun Zi directed.

sentences.zh: 監、令蓋自此始也。

translations.literal: supervisor and director probably began here.
translations.idiomatic: Those paired titles begin there.

sentences.zh: 及晉因之，並置員一人。

translations.literal: Jin continued it, each post holding one man.
translations.idiomatic: Jin kept one supervisor and one director.

sentences.zh: 中書侍郎，魏黃初初，中書既置監、令，又置通事郎，次黃門郎。

translations.literal: Palace Secretariat deputy—in Wei Huangchu at start, once Secretariat supervisor and director were set, general-affairs gentlemen were also placed, ranking below Yellow Gate gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Wei added general-affairs gentlemen under Yellow Gates once supervisor and director existed.

sentences.zh: 黃門郎已署事過，通事乃署名。

translations.literal: After Yellow Gate gentlemen finalized documents, general-affairs gentlemen signed.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow Gates finished drafts; general-affairs countersigned.

sentences.zh: 已署，奏以入，為帝省讀，書可。

translations.literal: Once signed, it was memorialized for entry; the emperor reviewed and marked approval.
translations.idiomatic: The packet then went to the throne for imperial 'approved.'

sentences.zh: 及晉，改曰中書侍郎，員四人。

translations.literal: Under Jin the name was changed to Palace Secretariat deputy; four posts.
translations.idiomatic: Jin renamed them Palace Secretariat deputies—four seats.

sentences.zh: 中書侍郎蓋此始也。

translations.literal: Palace Secretariat deputy probably began here.
translations.idiomatic: That is the origin of the deputy title.

sentences.zh: 及江左初，改中書侍郎曰通事郎，尋復為中書侍郎。

translations.literal: Early east of the Yangzi Palace Secretariat deputies were renamed general-affairs gentlemen; soon restored to Palace Secretariat deputy.
translations.idiomatic: The southern court briefly called them general-affairs gentlemen, then reverted.

sentences.zh: 中書舍人，案晉初初置舍人、通事各一人，江左合舍人通事謂之通事舍人，掌呈奏案章。

translations.literal: Palace Secretariat attendants—in tradition early Jin first set one attendant and one general-affairs messenger; east of the Yangzi combined attendant and general-affairs into general-affairs attendant, handling presentation of memorials and petitions.
translations.idiomatic: Early Jin paired one attendant with one messenger; south of the river merged them into general-affairs attendants who carried memorial folders to the throne.

sentences.zh: 後省，而以中書侍郎一人直西省，又掌詔命。

translations.literal: Later it was abolished, and one Palace Secretariat deputy rotated duty in the western bureau, also handling edicts and commands.
translations.idiomatic: They later folded the post; a single deputy minded the western bureau and drafted edicts.

sentences.zh: 秘書監，案漢桓帝延熹二年置秘書監，後省。

translations.literal: Director of the Palace Library—in tradition Emperor Huan of Han in the second year of Yanxi established a Palace Library director; later it was cut.
translations.idiomatic: Han Huan created a library director in 159 CE; the seat later vanished.

sentences.zh: 魏武為魏王，置秘書令、丞。

translations.literal: Wei Emperor Wu as Prince of Wei established Palace Secretary director and assistant.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao as Wei prince named a secretary director and deputy for archives.

sentences.zh: 及文帝黃初初，置中書令，典尚書奏事，而秘書改令為監。

translations.literal: When Wendi at the start of Huangchu established Palace Secretariat director to manage Secretariat memorial business, the Palace Secretary director title was changed to supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: Huangchu split drafting from archives: Zhongshu handled memorials while the old secretary director became library supervisor.

sentences.zh: 後以何禎為秘書丞，而秘書先自有丞，乃以禎為秘書右丞。

translations.literal: Later He Zhen was appointed Palace Library assistant, but the library already had an assistant; therefore Zhen was made Right Assistant of the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: He Zhen became library deputy while a deputy already existed—so he took the new right-deputy slot.

sentences.zh: 及晉受命，武帝以秘書並中書省，其秘書著作之局不廢。

translations.literal: When Jin received the mandate, Emperor Wu merged the Palace Library with the Palace Secretariat bureau, yet the library composition bureau was not abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Wudi folded library staff into the Zhongshu apparatus but kept the historiography office alive.

sentences.zh: 惠帝永平中，復置秘書監，其屬官有丞，有郎，並統著作省。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Hui in the Yongping era the Palace Library supervisor was restored; subordinate offices included assistants and gentlemen, jointly overseeing the Composition Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Huidi revived the library supervisor with deputies and gentlemen running the composition wing.

sentences.zh: 著作郎，周左史之任也。

translations.literal: Composition gentleman—it was the duty of Zhou's left historian.
translations.idiomatic: The compiler post echoed Zhou's left historian.

sentences.zh: 漢東京圖籍在東觀，故使名儒著作東觀，有其名，尚未有官。

translations.literal: Eastern Han kept maps and registers at the Eastern Observatory, so famed scholars composed texts there—there was a name but not yet an official post.
translations.idiomatic: Later Han parked archives at Eastern Observatory; luminaries wrote there long before the title existed.

sentences.zh: 魏明帝太和中，詔置著作郎，於此始有其官，隸中書省。

translations.literal: Wei Mingdi in the Taihe era issued an edict establishing composition gentlemen—here it first became an office, subordinate to the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Mingdi minted the composition gentleman title under Zhongshu.

sentences.zh: 及晉受命，武帝以繆徵為中書著作郎。

translations.literal: When Jin received the mandate, Emperor Wu appointed Miao Zheng as Palace Secretariat composition gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Wudi named Miao Zheng Zhongshu compiler.

sentences.zh: 元康二年，詔曰：「著作舊屬中書，而秘書既典文籍，今改中書著作為秘書著作。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuankang an edict said: "Composition formerly belonged to the Palace Secretariat; since the Palace Library already manages documents, now change Palace Secretariat composition to Palace Library composition.
translations.idiomatic: Yuankang edict moved compilers from Zhongshu to the library because archives lived there.

sentences.zh: 」於是改隸秘書省。

translations.literal: " Thus they were reassigned to the Palace Library bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Compilers henceforth answered to the library bureau.

sentences.zh: 後別自置省而猶隸秘書。

translations.literal: Later they separately established a bureau yet still reported to the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: They eventually spun up a dedicated bureau still under library oversight.

sentences.zh: 著作郎一人，謂之大著作郎，專掌史任，又置佐著作郎八人。

translations.literal: One composition gentleman was called senior composition gentleman, solely handling historical duty; eight assistant composition gentlemen were also appointed.
translations.idiomatic: One chief compiler ran history with eight assistants.

sentences.zh: 著作郎始到職，必撰名臣傳一人。

translations.literal: When composition gentlemen first took office they had to compose one biography of a celebrated minister.
translations.idiomatic: New compilers opened their tenure by drafting a notable minister biography.

sentences.zh: 太常、光祿勳、衛尉、太僕、廷尉、大鴻臚、宗正、大司農、少府、將作大匠、太后三卿、大長秋，皆為列卿，各置丞、功曹、主簿、五官等員。

translations.literal: Minister of Ceremonies, Imperial Coachman, Commandant of the Guards, Minister Coachman, Minister of Justice, Grand Herald, Director of Imperial Clan Affairs, Minister of Finance, Privy Treasurer, Corps of Palace Construction, the Three Ministers of the Empress Dowager, and Privy Treasurer of the Empress—all were column ministers; each had assistants, merit clerks, chief clerks, gatekeeper officers, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: The Nine Ministers plus empress-dowager and empress suites formed the column ministers—each with deputies, merit desks, chief clerks, and gate staff.

sentences.zh: 太常，有博士、協律校尉員，又統太學諸博士、祭酒及太史、太廟、太樂、鼓吹、陵等令，太史又別置靈台丞。

translations.literal: The Minister of Ceremonies had erudites and harmonics commandants on staff; also supervised Imperial Academy erudites and libationer, and directors for Astrology, Imperial Temple, Music, drum-and-pipe bands, mausolea—the Astrology Office additionally placed a Spirit Terrace assistant.
translations.idiomatic: Ceremonies oversaw classics professors, pitch pipes, the academy, temples, music, tombs, and a separate Spirit Terrace aide at astrology.

sentences.zh: 太常博士，魏官也。

translations.literal: Minister of Ceremonies erudites were Wei offices.
translations.idiomatic: Wei created the Ceremonies erudite posts.

sentences.zh: 魏文帝初置，晉因之。

translations.literal: Wei Wendi first established them; Jin continued.
translations.idiomatic: Wendi founded them; Jin kept them.

sentences.zh: 掌引導乘輿。

translations.literal: They guided and led the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: They escorted the sovereign's carriage.

sentences.zh: 王公已下應追諡者，則博士議定之。

translations.literal: For kings and dukes downward who merited posthumous epithets, the erudites deliberated and fixed them.
translations.idiomatic: Erudites voted posthumous styles for nobles.

sentences.zh: 協律校尉，漢協律都尉之職也，魏杜夔為之。

translations.literal: Harmonics commandant—it was the duty of Han's harmonics superintendent; Wei's Du Kui held it.
translations.idiomatic: The harmonics post descended from Han's pitch officer—Du Kui filled it under Wei.

sentences.zh: 及晉，改為協律校尉。

translations.literal: Under Jin it was changed to harmonics commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Jin retitled it harmonics commandant.

sentences.zh: 晉初承魏制，置博士十九人。

translations.literal: Early Jin inherited Wei regulations and established nineteen erudites.
translations.idiomatic: Early Jin kept nineteen classical chairs from Wei.

sentences.zh: 及咸甯四年，武帝初立國子學，定置國子祭酒、博士各一人，助教十五人，以教生徒。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xianning Emperor Wu first founded the Imperial Academy, fixing one libationer and one erudite each, fifteen teaching assistants, to instruct students.
translations.idiomatic: 278 CE launched the academy with one libationer, one professor, and fifteen assistants teaching disciples.

sentences.zh: 博士皆取履行清淳，通明典義者，若散騎常侍、中書侍郎、太子中庶子以上，乃得召試。

translations.literal: Erudites were all drawn from men of pure conduct who mastered canonical meaning; only those ranked elite cavalry standing attendant, Palace Secretariat deputy, heir-apparent household attendant or higher could be summoned to examination.
translations.idiomatic: Candidates needed pristine résumés and canonical mastery; only senior attendants and above sat the exam.

sentences.zh: 及江左初，減為九人。

translations.literal: Early east of the Yangzi it was reduced to nine.
translations.idiomatic: South of the river the corps shrank to nine chairs.

sentences.zh: 元帝末，增《儀禮》、《春秋公羊》博士各一人，合為十一人。

translations.literal: At the end of Emperor Yuan's reign one Ceremonies erudite each was added for Etiquette and Gongyang Commentary on the Spring and Autumn, totaling eleven.
translations.idiomatic: Late Yuandi added Etiquette and Gongyang chairs—eleven professors.

sentences.zh: 後又增為十六人，不復分掌《五經》，而謂之太學博士也。

translations.literal: Later it was increased to sixteen; they no longer split custody of the Five Classics but were called Imperial Academy erudites.
translations.idiomatic: The roster grew to sixteen unified professors rather than one canon each.

sentences.zh: 孝武太元十年，損國子助教員為十人。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu in the tenth year of Taiyuan cut Imperial Academy assistant posts to ten.
translations.idiomatic: 385 CE trimmed academy assistants to ten.

sentences.zh: 光祿勳，統武賁中郎將、羽林郎將、冗從僕射、羽林左監、五官左右中郎將、東園匠、太官，禦府、守宮、黃門、掖庭、清商、華林園、暴室等令。

translations.literal: The Imperial Coachman supervised tiger-ben guards director, feathered-forest commandant, supernumerary vice director, feathered-forest left intendant, gate defense left and right central commandants, eastern park craftsmen, imperial kitchens, wardrobe bureau, palace maintenance, Yellow Gates, lateral courts, Pure Music, imperial parks, sudden-arrest cells, and other directors.
translations.idiomatic: The Coachman ran imperial guards, feathered forest escorts, parks, kitchens, wardrobes, harem offices, music, gardens, and detention wards.

sentences.zh: 哀帝興寧二年，省光祿勳，並司徒。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xing'ning under Emperor Ai the Imperial Coachman was abolished and merged into the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: 364 CE folded Coachman into Education.

sentences.zh: 孝武甯康元年復置。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu in the first year of Ningkang restored it.
translations.idiomatic: 373 CE revived the Coachman.

sentences.zh: 衛尉，統武庫、公車、衛士、諸冶等令，左右都候，南北東西督冶掾。

translations.literal: The Commandant of the Guards supervised arsenal, public carriage office, garrison commandants, various foundry directors, left and right capital patrols, and north-south-east-west foundry clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Guards ran armories, carriages, foundries, patrols, and regional forge desks.

sentences.zh: 及渡江，省衛尉。

translations.literal: After crossing the Yangzi the Commandant of the Guards was cut.
translations.idiomatic: South of the river they struck the guards commandant.

sentences.zh: 太僕，統典農、典虞都尉，典虞丞，左右中典牧都尉，車府典牧，乘黃廄、驊騮廄、龍馬廄等令。

translations.literal: The Minister Coachman supervised colony commandants, herd commandants and assistants, left-right-central herd commandants, chariot office herd masters, directors for bay horses, splendid bays, dragon-horse bays, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: Coachman oversaw herds, transport animals, and stable masters.

sentences.zh: 典牧又別置羊牧丞。

translations.literal: The herd office additionally placed a sheep-herd assistant.
translations.idiomatic: Herds added a sheep deputy.

sentences.zh: 太僕，自元帝渡江之後或省或置。

translations.literal: The Minister Coachman after Emperor Yuan crossed the Yangzi was sometimes cut, sometimes restored.
translations.idiomatic: South of the river the Coachman flickered on and off.

sentences.zh: 太僕省，故驊騮為門下之職。

translations.literal: When Minister Coachman was cut, therefore splendid bay belonged to gate-affairs duty.
translations.idiomatic: Without a Coachman the splendid stable fell under gate affairs.

sentences.zh: 廷尉，主刑法獄訟，屬官有正、監、評，並有律博士員。

translations.literal: The Minister of Justice presided over penal law and litigation; subordinates included directors rectifying, supervising, and reviewing cases, with legal erudites on staff.
translations.idiomatic: Justice handled crime and trials with rectifiers, reviewers, and statute professors.

sentences.zh: 大鴻臚，統大行、典客、園池、華林園、鉤盾等令，又有青宮列丞、鄴玄武苑丞。

translations.literal: The Grand Herald supervised grand envoy, guest receptions, imperial parks, imperial gardens, hook-shield offices, and other directors; there were also Azure Palace column assistants and Ye northern-dark garden assistants.
translations.idiomatic: The Herald ran diplomacy, parks, gardens, and palace annex offices.

sentences.zh: 及江左，有事則權置，無事則省。

translations.literal: East of the Yangzi it was provisionally set when needed and cut when quiet.
translations.idiomatic: South of the river the Herald appeared only when busy.

sentences.zh: 宗正，統皇族宗人圖諜，又統太醫令史，又有司牧掾員。
