translations.literal: The Director of Imperial Clan Affairs supervised imperial clan registers and genealogy; also supervised imperial physicians and clerks; there were also herd clerks on staff.
translations.idiomatic: Clan affairs kept lineage rolls, court physicians, and pasture deputies.

sentences.zh: 及渡江，哀帝省並太常，太醫以給門下省。

translations.literal: After crossing the Yangzi Emperor Ai merged it into Ceremonies; imperial physicians went to the Gate Affairs bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Aidi folded Clan into Ceremonies and lent physicians to gate affairs.

sentences.zh: 大司農，統太倉、籍田、導官三令，襄國都水長，東西南北部護漕掾。

translations.literal: The Minister of Finance supervised granary, sacred-field, and mill directors, Xiangguo water-intendant chief, and east-west-north-south grain convoy clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Finance ran granaries, sacred fields, milling, and canal convoys.

sentences.zh: 及渡江，哀帝省並都水，孝武復置。

translations.literal: After crossing the Yangzi Emperor Ai merged it into the Water Superintendent; Emperor Xiaowu restored it.
translations.idiomatic: South of the river Aidi merged Finance into hydraulics; Xiaowu split them again.

sentences.zh: 少府，統材官校尉、中左右三尚方、中黃左右藏、左校、甄官、平准、奚官等令，左校坊、鄴中黃左右藏、油官等丞。

translations.literal: The Privy Treasurer supervised works commandant, left-center-right Upper Workshops, inner-yellow left-right treasuries, left works, pottery office, market balancer, palace artisans, and other directors; left works compound, Ye inner-yellow treasuries, oil offices, and other assistants.
translations.idiomatic: Treasury oversaw workshops, treasuries, crafts, markets, and palace industries.

sentences.zh: 及渡江，哀帝省並丹陽尹，孝武復置。

translations.literal: After crossing the Yangzi Emperor Ai merged it into the governor of Danyang; Emperor Xiaowu restored it.
translations.idiomatic: Aidi folded Treasury into Danyang governor; Xiaowu revived it.

sentences.zh: 自渡江唯置一尚方，又省禦府。

translations.literal: Since crossing the Yangzi only one Upper Workshop remained; wardrobe bureau was also cut.
translations.idiomatic: South of the river kept a single workshop and dropped wardrobe.

sentences.zh: 將作大匠，有事則置，無事則罷。

translations.literal: Corps of Palace Construction was set when there was business and dismissed when idle.
translations.idiomatic: The palace builders appeared only for projects.

sentences.zh: 太后三卿，衛尉、少府、太僕，漢置，皆隨太后宮為官號，在同名卿上，無太后則闕。

translations.literal: The Three Ministers of the Empress Dowager—Commandant of the Guards, Privy Treasurer, Minister Coachman—Han established them; all followed the empress dowager's palace as title designations, ranking above ministers of the same name; when there was no empress dowager they stayed vacant.
translations.idiomatic: Han titled empress-dowager suites above homonymous ministers; without a dowager the seats stayed empty.

sentences.zh: 魏改漢制，在九卿下。

translations.literal: Wei altered Han regulations, placing them below the Nine Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Wei ranked dowager ministers under the Nine Ministers.

sentences.zh: 及晉復舊，在同號卿上。

translations.literal: When Jin restored the old pattern they again ranked above same-title ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Jin returned them above peers with identical names.

sentences.zh: 大長秋，皇后卿也，有後則置，無後則省。

translations.literal: Grand Privy Treasurer of the Empress—it was the empress's minister; established when there was an empress, cut when none.
translations.idiomatic: The empress steward existed only when a consort reigned.

sentences.zh: 治書侍御史，案漢宣帝幸宣室齋居而決事，令侍御史二人治書侍側，後因別置，謂之治書侍御史，蓋其始也。

translations.literal: Law-editing attendant censor—in tradition Emperor Xuan of Han held court fasting in the Basilica and decided cases, ordering two attendant censors to edit documents at his side; afterward they were separately established—called law-editing attendant censors—probably beginning here.
translations.idiomatic: Han Xuan's Basilica sessions spawned side clerks who became law-editing censors.

sentences.zh: 及魏，又置治書執法，掌奏劾，而治書侍御史掌律令，二官俱置。

translations.literal: Under Wei law-enforcement editors were also established to handle impeachment memorials while law-editing attendant censors handled statutes—both offices existed.
translations.idiomatic: Wei paired jurisprudence censors with impeachment editors.

sentences.zh: 及晉，唯置治書侍御史，員四人。

translations.literal: Under Jin only law-editing attendant censors remained—four posts.
translations.idiomatic: Jin kept four law-editing censors only.

sentences.zh: 泰始四年，又置黃沙獄治書侍御史一人，秩與中丞同，掌詔獄及廷尉不當者皆治之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taishi another Yellow Sands prison law-editing attendant censor was added at salary matching the assistant director, handling imperial-order prisons and correcting injustice from the Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: 268 CE added a Yellow Sands censor equal to the assistant director for edict prisons and judicial appeal.

sentences.zh: 後並河南，遂省黃沙治書侍御史。

translations.literal: Later when merged with Henan the Yellow Sands law-editing attendant censor was cut.
translations.idiomatic: Once Henan merged in, Yellow Sands censors vanished.

sentences.zh: 及太康中，又省治書侍御史二員。

translations.literal: During Taikang two law-editing attendant censors were again cut.
translations.idiomatic: Taikang trimmed two law editors.

sentences.zh: 侍御史，案二漢所掌凡有五曹：一曰令曹，掌律令；

translations.literal: Attendant censors—in tradition Former and Later Han supervised five divisions: first called Statutes Division, handling statutes and ordinances;
translations.idiomatic: Han censors ran five desks—statutes first;

sentences.zh: 二曰印曹，掌刻印；

translations.literal: second called Seals Division, handling seal carving;
translations.idiomatic: seals second;

sentences.zh: 三曰供曹，掌齋祠；

translations.literal: third called Supplies Division, handling fasting sacrifices;
translations.idiomatic: supplies third;

sentences.zh: 四曰尉馬曹，掌廄馬；

translations.literal: fourth called Stable Horses Division, handling stable horses;
translations.idiomatic: stables fourth;

sentences.zh: 五曰乘曹，掌護駕。

translations.literal: fifth called Riding Division, handling imperial escort.
translations.idiomatic: escort fifth.

sentences.zh: 魏置八人。

translations.literal: Wei established eight.
translations.idiomatic: Wei ran eight censors.

sentences.zh: 及晉，置員九人，品同治書，而有十三曹：吏曹、課第曹、直事曹、印曹、中都督曹、外都督曹、媒曹、符節曹、水曹、中壘曹、營軍曹、法曹、算曹。

translations.literal: Under Jin nine posts were established, grade matching law editors, yet there were thirteen divisions: Personnel, Merit Ranking, Duty Affairs, Seals, Inner Area Command, Outer Area Command, Matchmaking, Tallies, Water, Inner Rampart, Camp Army, Law, Arithmetic.
translations.idiomatic: Jin fielded nine men across thirteen desks—personnel through arithmetic.

sentences.zh: 及江左初，省課第曹，置庫曹，掌廄牧牛馬市租，後分曹，置外左庫、內左庫雲。

translations.literal: Early east of the Yangzi Merit Ranking was cut and Storehouse added for stable herds, cattle, horses, and market rents; later the division split into outer-left and inner-left storehouses.
translations.idiomatic: South of the river swapped merit rankings for storehouse desks tracking herds and rents, later splitting inner and outer vaults.

sentences.zh: 殿中侍御史，案魏蘭台遣二御史居殿中，伺察非法，即其始也。

translations.literal: Palace hall attendant censors—in tradition Wei's Orchid Terrace dispatched two censors inside the palace hall to watch for illegality—probably beginning here.
translations.idiomatic: Wei placed hall watchers from the Orchid Terrace.

sentences.zh: 及晉，置四人，江左置二人。

translations.literal: Under Jin four were established; east of the Yangzi two.
translations.idiomatic: Jin used four hall censors; south of the river two.

sentences.zh: 又案魏晉官品令又有禁防禦史第七品，孝武太元中有檢校御史吳琨，則此二職亦蘭台之職也。

translations.literal: Moreover Wei-Jin rank regulations also listed defense censors at seventh grade; during Emperor Xiaowu's Taiyuan era inspector-censor Wu Kun appeared—thus both posts belonged to Orchid Terrace duties.
translations.idiomatic: Rank lists included defense and inspector censors—Wu Kun shows both stayed under the terrace.

sentences.zh: 符節御史，秦符璽令之職也。

translations.literal: Tally censor—it was the duty of Qin's tally director.
translations.idiomatic: Tally censors descended from Qin's seal office.

sentences.zh: 漢因之，位次御史中丞。

translations.literal: Han continued it, ranking below the assistant director.
translations.idiomatic: Han ranked them under the assistant director.

sentences.zh: 至魏，別為一台，位次御史中丞，掌授節、銅武符、竹使符。

translations.literal: By Wei it became a separate bureau ranking below the assistant director, managing issuance of credentials, bronze martial tallies, and bamboo mission tallies.
translations.idiomatic: Wei gave tallies its own desk below the assistant director for seals and tokens.

sentences.zh: 及泰始九年，武帝省並蘭台，置符節御史掌其事焉。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Taishi Emperor Wu merged it into the Orchid Terrace and established tally censors to manage those affairs.
translations.idiomatic: 273 CE folded tally duty back into the terrace.

sentences.zh: 司隸校尉，案漢武初置十三州，刺史各一人，又置司隸校尉，察三輔、三河、弘農七郡，曆漢東京及魏晉，其官不替。

translations.literal: Regional Inspector—in tradition Emperor Wu of Han first established thirteen provinces with one inspector each; also established the Metropolitan Superintendent to inspect three metropolitan districts, three river circuits, and Hongnong—seven commanderies; through Later Han Eastern Han and Wei-Jin the office continued unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Han's provincial inspectors plus the capital superintendent endured through Wei and Jin.

sentences.zh: 屬官有功曹、都官從事、諸曹從事、部郡從事、主簿、錄事、門下書佐、省事、記室書佐、諸曹書佐守從事、武猛從事等員，凡吏一百人，卒三十二人。

translations.literal: Subordinate offices included merit clerk, capital clerk, various bureau clerks, commandery clerks, chief clerk, recorder, gate document clerks, miscellaneous clerks, secretary clerks, various bureau clerks including guards and clerks—in all one hundred clerks and thirty-two runners.
translations.idiomatic: Staff topped out at one hundred clerks and thirty-two runners across myriad desks.

sentences.zh: 及渡江，乃罷司隸校尉官，其職乃揚州刺史也。

translations.literal: After crossing the Yangzi the Metropolitan Superintendent post was abolished; its duties fell to the governor of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: South of the river Yangzhou's governor absorbed metropolitan supervision.

sentences.zh: 謁者僕射，秦官也，自漢至魏因之。

translations.literal: Chief usher—it was a Qin office; from Han through Wei it continued.
translations.idiomatic: Chief usher came from Qin through Wei.

sentences.zh: 魏置僕射，掌大拜授及百官班次，統謁者十人。

translations.literal: Wei established chief steward directing grand investitures and court seating order, supervising ten ushers.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's chief steward staged audiences and lineups with ten ushers.

sentences.zh: 及武帝省僕射，以謁者並蘭台。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu cut chief steward, ushers merged into the Orchid Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: Wudi merged ushers into the terrace.

sentences.zh: 江左復置僕射，後又省。

translations.literal: East of the Yangzi chief steward was restored; later cut again.
translations.idiomatic: South of the river restored then dropped the steward.

sentences.zh: 都水使者，漢水衡之職也。

translations.literal: Water superintendent envoy—it was Han's superintendent of waters duty.
translations.idiomatic: The water envoy continued Han's hydraulic commissioner.

sentences.zh: 漢又有都水長丞，主陂池灌溉，保守河渠，屬太常。

translations.literal: Han also had chief and assistant water intendants managing dikes, irrigation, and river conservation under Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: Han tasked Ceremonies with dikes and canals via water intendants.

sentences.zh: 漢東京省都水，置河堤謁者，魏因之。

translations.literal: Eastern Han cut unified water office and placed river-dike ushers; Wei continued.
translations.idiomatic: Later Han switched to dike ushers; Wei kept them.

sentences.zh: 及武帝省水衡，置都水使者一人，以河堤謁者為都水官屬。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu cut the superintendent of waters he established one water superintendent envoy, making river-dike ushers subordinates of water offices.
translations.idiomatic: Wudi replaced the old water ministry with one envoy over dike officers.

sentences.zh: 及江左，省河堤謁者，置謁者六人。

translations.literal: East of the Yangzi river-dike ushers were cut and six ushers were placed.
translations.idiomatic: South of the river swapped dike ushers for six general ushers.

sentences.zh: 左右衛將軍，案文帝初置中衛。

translations.literal: Left and Right Guards generals—in tradition Wendi first established Central Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Wendi founded the central guard corps.

sentences.zh: 及武帝受命，分為左右衛，以羊琇為左、趙序為右。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu received the mandate he divided them into Left and Right Guards, appointing Yang Xiu left and Zhao Xu right.
translations.idiomatic: Wudi split Central Guard into left under Yang Xiu and right under Zhao Xu.

sentences.zh: 並置長史、司馬、功曹、主薄員，江左罷長史。

translations.literal: Chief clerk, adjutant, merit clerk, and chief scribe were both established; east of the Yangzi chief clerk was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Each guard had full staff; south of the river dropped chief clerks.

sentences.zh: 驍騎將軍、遊擊將軍，並漢雜號將軍也。

translations.literal: Valiant Cavalry general and Mobile Corps general—both were Han miscellaneous-number generals.
translations.idiomatic: Valiant cavalry and mobile corps were Han-style misc generals.

sentences.zh: 魏置為中軍。

translations.literal: Wei established them as central army.
translations.idiomatic: Wei folded them into the central army.

sentences.zh: 及晉，以領、護、左右衛、驍騎、遊擊為六軍。

translations.literal: Under Jin, Colonel Directors, Colonel Protectors, Left and Right Guards, Valiant Cavalry, and Mobile Corps formed the Six Armies.
translations.idiomatic: Jin counted directors, protectors, both guards, valiant cavalry, and mobile corps as the six armies.

sentences.zh: 左右前後軍將軍，案魏明帝時有左軍，則左軍魏官也，至晉不改。

translations.literal: Left, Right, Front, Rear army generals—in tradition Wei Mingdi had a Left Army, so Left Army was a Wei office; unchanged through Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Mingdi invented the left army; Jin kept the pattern.

sentences.zh: 武帝初又置前軍、右軍，泰始八年又置後軍，是為四軍。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu at the beginning also established Front Army and Right Army; in the eighth year of Taishi Rear Army was again established—thus the four armies.
translations.idiomatic: Wudi first created front and right field armies; adding the rear in 272 completed the four.

sentences.zh: 屯騎、步兵、越騎、長水、射聲等校尉，是為五校，並漢官也。

translations.literal: Garrison Cavalry, Infantry, Crack Cavalry, Long River, and Thunderbolt Shoot commandants formed the Five Camps—all Han offices.
translations.idiomatic: The five camps—garrison cavalry through thunderbolt—were Han units.

sentences.zh: 魏晉逮于江左，猶領營兵，並置司馬、功曹、主簿。

translations.literal: From Wei-Jin down to the Jiang left they still commanded camp troops and each had adjutant, merit clerk, and chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Wei-Jin camps kept soldiers with adjutants and clerks.

sentences.zh: 後省左軍、右軍、前軍、後軍為鎮衛軍，其左右營校尉自如舊，皆中領軍統之。

translations.literal: Later Left, Right, Front, Rear armies were cut into Garrison Guard armies; left and right camp commandants followed old regulations, all commanded by the Central Colonel Director.
translations.idiomatic: Directional armies merged into guard commands still overseen by the central colonel.

sentences.zh: 二衛始制前驅、由基、強弩為三部司馬，各置督史。

translations.literal: The Two Guards first instituted Van, Youji, and Strong Crossbow as three divisions of adjutants, each with supervising clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Both guards organized van guard, Youji archers, and strong crossbow divisions—each with overseers.

sentences.zh: 左衛，熊渠武賁；

translations.literal: Left Guard—Xiongqu tiger-ben;
translations.idiomatic: The left guard drew Bear-Gully royal guards;

sentences.zh: 右衛，佽飛武賁。

translations.literal: Right Guard—Cifei tiger-ben.
translations.idiomatic: the right guard drew Feiyi swimmers.

sentences.zh: 二衛各五部督。

translations.literal: The Two Guards each had five division supervisors.
translations.idiomatic: Each guard deployed five division overseers.

sentences.zh: 其命中武賁，驍騎、遊擊各領之。

translations.literal: As for accurate-shot tiger-ben, Valiant Cavalry and Mobile Corps each commanded them.
translations.idiomatic: Crack-shot guards answered to valiant cavalry and mobile corps.

sentences.zh: 又置武賁、羽林、上騎、異力四部，並命中為五督。

translations.literal: Tiger-ben, feathered forest, superior cavalry, and extraordinary strength formed four divisions; together with accurate-shot they made five supervised divisions.
translations.idiomatic: Tiger guards, feathered forest, elite riders, and picked strongmen joined crack shots as five commands.

sentences.zh: 其衛、鎮四軍如五校，各置千人。

translations.literal: The Guard and Garrison four armies matched the Five Camps—each established one thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Guard and field armies mirrored the five camps at one thousand troops each.

sentences.zh: 更制殿中將軍，中郎、校尉、司馬比驍騎。

translations.literal: Palace hall generals were reformed; gentlemen-of-the-palace, commandants, and adjutants ranked alongside Valiant Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Hall generals, palace gentlemen, and camp officers matched valiant-cavalry grade.

sentences.zh: 持椎斧武賁，分屬二衛。

translations.literal: Mace-and-axe tiger-ben were divided between the Two Guards.
translations.idiomatic: Ax-wielding tiger guards split between both guards.

sentences.zh: 尉中武賁、持鈒冗從、羽林司馬，常從人數各有差。

translations.literal: Palace tiger-ben, dagger-axe supernumerary followers, feathered-forest adjutants—regular escort complements varied by detail.
translations.idiomatic: Hall guards, axe escorts, and feathered-forest adjutants carried differing standing complements.

sentences.zh: 武帝甚重兵官，故軍校多選朝廷清望之士居之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu greatly esteemed military officers; therefore army-school posts often selected eminent worthies from court.
translations.idiomatic: Wudi prized martial appointments and stacked camps with respected courtiers.

sentences.zh: 先是，陳勰為文帝所待，特有才用，明解軍令。

translations.literal: Earlier Chen Xie had been favored by Emperor Wen, unusually talented and skilled, clearly understanding military regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xie enjoyed Wendi's favor—acute on army regulations.

sentences.zh: 帝為晉王，委任使典兵事。

translations.literal: When the emperor was Prince of Jin he entrusted him to manage military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: As Prince of Jin he ran forces for the future emperor.

sentences.zh: 及蜀破後，令勰受諸葛亮圍陣用兵倚伏之法，又甲乙校標幟之制，勰悉暗練之，遂以勰為殿中典兵中郎將，遷將軍。

translations.literal: After Shu fell he ordered Xie to receive Zhuge Liang's encirclement formations and maneuver secrets of troops and ambush, as well as the first-second camp banner systems—Xie mastered them all in darkness; therefore Xie was made palace hall gentleman commanding troops as gentleman-of-the-palace, later promoted general.
translations.idiomatic: After Shu's fall Chen Xie absorbed Zhuge Liang's formations and dual-camp signals—Wudi made him hall corps gentleman then general.

sentences.zh: 久之，武帝每出入，勰持白獸幡在乘輿左右，鹵簿陳列齊肅。

translations.literal: After a long time, whenever Emperor Wu went out Xie held the white beast banner beside the imperial carriage; the guard of honor arrayed itself perfectly solemn.
translations.idiomatic: For years Chen Xie bore the white beast banner beside the coach—his drills stayed razor sharp.

sentences.zh: 太康末，武帝嘗出射雉，勰時已為都水使者，散從。

translations.literal: Near the end of Taikang Emperor Wu once went out to shoot pheasants; Xie by then was water superintendent envoy, following loosely.
translations.idiomatic: Late Taikang Wudi hunted pheasants while Chen Xie, now water envoy, tagged along.

sentences.zh: 車駕逼暗乃還，漏已盡，當合函，停乘輿，良久不得合，乃詔勰合之。

translations.literal: The carriage turned back only when dusk pressed close; the clepsydra had run out—it should have closed the armored coach-box; they halted the imperial carriage; long unable to close it—thereupon an edict ordered Xie to close it.
translations.idiomatic: Nightfall stranded the train past water-clock closing time—the royal coach shell stuck open until Wudi told Chen Xie to seal it.

sentences.zh: 勰舉白獸幡指麾，須臾之間而函成。

translations.literal: Xie raised the white beast banner and directed; in an instant the coach-box was closed.
translations.idiomatic: He waved the banner and snapped the coach shell shut.

sentences.zh: 皆謝勰閑解，甚為武帝所任。

translations.literal: All thanked Xie for his practiced skill; he was greatly trusted by Emperor Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Onlookers praised his practiced hand; Wudi relied on him heavily.

sentences.zh: 太子太傅、少傅，皆古官也。

translations.literal: Grand tutor and junior tutor of the heir apparent—both were ancient offices.
translations.idiomatic: Heir tutors were classical posts.

sentences.zh: 泰始三年，武帝始建官，各置一人，尚未置詹事，官事無大小，皆由二傅，並有功曹、主簿、五官。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taishi Emperor Wu first established the offices, each one post; not yet appointing a household supervisor—office business large or small all passed through the two tutors, who also had merit clerks, chief clerks, and gatekeeper officers.
translations.idiomatic: 267 CE created paired tutors before any household supervisor—every detail ran through them with full clerical staff.

sentences.zh: 太傅中二千石，少傅二千石。

translations.literal: Grand tutor at salary comparable to two thousand shi; junior tutor at two thousand shi.
translations.idiomatic: Senior tutor drew near two thousand shi; junior tutor two thousand.

sentences.zh: 其訓導者，太傅在前，少傅在後。

translations.literal: Those who instructed—grand tutor in front, junior tutor behind.
translations.idiomatic: Instruction lined up senior tutor forward, junior aft.

sentences.zh: 皇太子先拜，諸傅然後答之。

translations.literal: The imperial heir first bowed; the tutors then answered.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince bowed first; tutors returned the courtesy.

sentences.zh: 武帝后以儲副體尊，遂命諸公居之；

translations.literal: Later Emperor Wu because the heir's station was august ordered various dukes to occupy the posts;
translations.idiomatic: Once the heir's rank swelled, grandees filled those chairs;

sentences.zh: 以本位重，故或行或領。

translations.literal: because the posts were weighty, therefore some served in person and some held concurrent titles.
translations.idiomatic: weight meant some served full-time, some doubled other posts.

sentences.zh: 時侍中任愷，武帝所親敬，復使領之，蓋一時之制也。

translations.literal: At the time attendant Ren Kai, whom Emperor Wu personally favored and respected, was also made to oversee them—probably an arrangement of the moment.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Kai briefly doubled duty—a court expedient.

sentences.zh: 咸甯元年，以給事黃門侍郎楊珧為詹事，掌宮事，二傅不復領官屬。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianning gentleman attendant at the Yellow Gates Yang Yao was made household supervisor handling palace business; the two tutors no longer supervised subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: 275 CE Yang Yao became household supervisor so tutors shed staff.

sentences.zh: 及楊珧為衛將軍，領少傅，省詹事，遂崇廣傅訓，命太尉賈充領太保，司空齊王攸領太傅，所置吏屬復如舊。

translations.literal: When Yang Yao became guards general holding junior tutor, household supervisor was cut; tutor instruction was then enlarged—Minister of War Jia Chong was ordered to hold senior guardian, Prince You of Qi to hold grand tutor; appointed clerical staff returned as before.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yao's promotion restored tutor suites under Jia Chong and Sima You.

sentences.zh: 二傅進賢兩梁冠，黑介幘，五時朝服，佩水蒼玉，食奉日三斛。

translations.literal: The two tutors wore two-beam advanced-worth caps, black scarves, five-seasons court dress, dark aquamarine jade, daily grain allowance three hu.
translations.idiomatic: Tutors wore two-ridged caps, black kerchiefs, seasonal robes, jade, three hu daily.

sentences.zh: 太康二年，始給春賜絹五十匹，秋絹百匹，綿百斤。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taikang they began granting spring silk fifty bolts, autumn silk one hundred bolts, cotton one hundred jin.
translations.idiomatic: 281 CE added seasonal silk and cotton allotments.

sentences.zh: 其後太尉汝南王亮、車騎將軍楊駿、司空衛瓘、石鑒皆領傅保，猶不置詹事，以終武帝之世。

translations.literal: Afterward Minister of War Prince Liang of Runan, chariots general Yang Jun, Minister of Works Wei Guan, and Shi Jian all held tutor-guardian posts; still no household supervisor through Emperor Wu's reign.
translations.idiomatic: Grandees doubled as tutors but no household supervisor until Huidi.

sentences.zh: 惠帝元康元年，復置詹事，二傅給菜田六頃，田騶六人，立夏後不及田者，食奉一年。

translations.literal: Emperor Hui in the first year of Yuankang restored household supervisor; the two tutors received six qing vegetable land and six field runners; if after beginning of summer land had not been awarded, one year's salary instead.
translations.idiomatic: 291 CE revived the supervisor and granted tutors vegetable plots like ministers.

sentences.zh: 置丞一人，秩千石；

translations.literal: One assistant was placed at rank one thousand shi;
translations.idiomatic: One deputy at one thousand shi;

sentences.zh: 主簿、五官掾、功曹史、主記門下史、錄事、戶曹法曹倉曹賊曹功曹書佐、門下亭長、門下書佐、省事各一人，給赤耳安車一乘。

translations.literal: chief clerk, gatekeeper officers, merit clerk, chief recorder, gate clerks, recorder, household office, law office, granary office, thieves office, merit clerk assistants, gate precinct chief, gate document clerks, miscellaneous clerks—one each; one red-eared secure carriage granted.
translations.idiomatic: full tutor household staff plus a red-eared carriage.

sentences.zh: 及湣懷建官，乃置六傅，三太、三少，以景帝諱師，故改太師為太保，通省尚書事，詹事文書關由六傅。

translations.literal: When Crown Prince Minhuai established offices, six tutors were set—three senior and three junior—because of the taboo on Emperor Jing's name Shi, therefore Grand Instructor was changed to senior guardian, jointly overseeing Secretariat business; household paperwork passed through all six tutors.
translations.idiomatic: Minhuai's six tutors—taboo turned instructor into guardian—shared Secretariat oversight.

sentences.zh: 然自元康之後，諸傅或二或三，或四或六，及永康中復不置詹事也。

translations.literal: Yet from Yuankang onward tutors numbered two, three, four, or six; by Yongkang household supervisor was again absent.
translations.idiomatic: Tutor counts fluctuated; Yongkang dropped the supervisor again.

sentences.zh: 自太安已來置詹事，終孝懷之世。

translations.literal: From Tai'an onward household supervisor was set through Emperor Xiaohuai's reign.
translations.idiomatic: Tai'an forward kept supervisors through the prince's fall.

sentences.zh: 渡江之後，有太傅少傅，不立師保。

translations.literal: After crossing the Yangzi there were grand and junior tutors but no instructor or guardian titles.
translations.idiomatic: South of the river kept grand and junior tutors only.

sentences.zh: 中庶子四人，職如侍中。

translations.literal: Four household attendants—duty like palace attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Four inner household attendants matched palace attendants.

sentences.zh: 中舍人四人，咸寧四年置，以舍人才學美者為之，與中庶子共掌文翰，職如黃門侍郎，在中庶子下，洗馬上。

translations.literal: Four household gentlemen—established fourth year of Xianning; men of literary talent among gentlemen held them; together with household attendants they managed documents—duty like Yellow Gate gentlemen, below household attendants, above groom.
translations.idiomatic: 278 CE added talented gentlemen under attendants, above grooms, drafting documents.

sentences.zh: 食官令一人，職如太官令。

translations.literal: One victualing director—duty like imperial kitchen director.
translations.idiomatic: One food steward like the imperial chef.

sentences.zh: 庶子四人，職比散騎常侍、中書監令。

translations.literal: Four gentlemen—duty comparable to elite cavalry standing attendant and Palace Secretariat supervisor or director.
translations.idiomatic: Four gentlemen matched standing attendants or Zhongshu leaders.

sentences.zh: 舍人十六人，職比散騎、中書等侍郎。

translations.literal: Sixteen gentlemen—duty comparable to elite cavalry and Zhongshu deputies.
translations.idiomatic: Sixteen gentlemen equaled deputy-tier posts.

sentences.zh: 洗馬八人，職如謁者秘書，掌圖籍。

translations.literal: Eight grooms—duty like ushers and secretaries, managing maps and registers.
translations.idiomatic: Eight grooms handled archives like secretariat ushers.

sentences.zh: 釋奠講經則掌其事，出則直者前驅，導威儀。

translations.literal: For libation rites and lecturing on classics they managed the event; when going out the duty man rode vanguard guiding ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: They staged classics ceremonies and led processions when the heir traveled.

sentences.zh: 率更令，主宮殿門戶及賞罰事，職如光祿勳、衛尉。

translations.literal: Pitch-pipe director—managed palace gates and rewards or punishments—duty like Imperial Coachman and Commandant of the Guards.
translations.idiomatic: The pitch director watched gates and discipline like Coachman and Guards.

sentences.zh: 家令，主刑獄、穀貨、飲食，職比司農、少府。

translations.literal: Household steward—managed criminal cases, grain and goods, food and drink—duty comparable to Minister of Finance and Privy Treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: The steward ran justice and pantry like Finance and Treasury.

sentences.zh: 漢東京主食官令，食官令及晉自為官，不復屬家令。

translations.literal: Eastern Han took household victualing director as chief; victualing director under Jin became its own office, no longer under household steward.
translations.idiomatic: Later Han tied food to the steward; Jin detached the kitchen office.

sentences.zh: 僕，主車馬、親族，職如太僕、宗正。

translations.literal: Steward assistant—managed chariots, horses, and kin—duty like Minister Coachman and Director of Imperial Clan Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The assistant handled transport and kin like Coachman and Clan director.

sentences.zh: 左右衛率，案武帝建東宮，置衛率，初曰中衛率。

translations.literal: Left and Right Guard rates—when Emperor Wu built the Eastern Palace he set guard rates, first called Central Guard Rate.
translations.idiomatic: Wudi's heir's palace began with a central guard rate.

sentences.zh: 泰始五年，分為左右，各領一軍。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taishi they were divided into left and right, each commanding one army.
translations.idiomatic: 269 CE split them into left and right armies.

sentences.zh: 惠帝時，湣懷太子在東宮，又加前後二率。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Hui Crown Prince Minhuai in the Eastern Palace added front and rear rates.
translations.idiomatic: Huidi's heir added front and rear guard commands.

sentences.zh: 及江左，省前後二率，孝武太元中又置。

translations.literal: East of the Yangzi front and rear were cut; Emperor Xiaowu in Taiyuan restored them.
translations.idiomatic: South of the river dropped front/rear until Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 王置師、友、文學各一人，景帝諱，故改師為傅。

translations.literal: Princes set instructor, companion, and scholar—one each; because of Emperor Jing's taboo instructor was changed to tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Princes gained tutor, friend, and scholar—'instructor' became 'tutor' for taboo.

sentences.zh: 友者因文王、仲尼四友之名號。

translations.literal: Companion takes the name from King Wen and Confucius's four companions.
translations.idiomatic: The 'friend' title echoed Confucius's four companions.

sentences.zh: 改太守為內史，省相及僕。

translations.literal: Governors were changed to interior stewards; chancellor and steward assistant were cut.
translations.idiomatic: Governors became interior stewards; chancellor and assistant dropped.

sentences.zh: 有郎中令、中尉、大農為三卿。

translations.literal: Palace intendant, commandant, and grand agronomist formed three ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Three minister slots: intendant, commandant, grand agronomist.

sentences.zh: 大國置左右常侍各一人，省郎中，置侍郎二人，典書、典祠、典衛、學官令、典書丞各一人，治書四人，中尉司馬、世子庶子、陵廟牧長各一人，謁者四人，中大夫六人，舍人十人，典府各一人。

translations.literal: Large principalities set left and right permanent attendants one each; palace gentlemen were cut and two gentlemen placed; classics, sacrifices, guards, academy directors, classics assistants one each; law editors four; commandant adjutant, heir's gentleman, mausoleum pasture chief one each; ushers four, grand gentlemen six, gentlemen ten, treasury stewards one each.
translations.idiomatic: Large fiefs listed full courts—down to ten gentlemen and treasury aides.

sentences.zh: 咸甯三年，衛將軍楊珧與中書監荀勖以齊王攸有時望，懼惠帝有後難，因追故司空裴秀立五等封建之旨，從容共陳時宜於武帝，以為「古者建侯，所以籓衛王室。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianning Guards General Yang Yao and Palace Secretariat supervisor Xun Xu, because Prince You of Qi enjoyed timely prestige and feared later troubles for Emperor Hui, following former Minister of Works Pei Xiu's intent to establish five-grade feudal ranks, calmly presented contemporary policy to Emperor Wu, saying "In antiquity establishing nobility was to screen and guard the royal house.
translations.idiomatic: 277 CE Yang Yao and Xun Xu cited Pei Xiu's feudal plan, warning Wudi about princely power.

sentences.zh: 今吳寇未殄，方岳任大，而諸王為帥，都督封國，既各不臣其統內，於事重非宜。

translations.literal: Now Wu bandits are not yet destroyed; regional posts are weighty; yet various princes serve as commanders, supervising fiefs—each not treating subordinates within his command as subjects—in affairs this is seriously inappropriate.
translations.idiomatic: They argued Wu remained and princes commanding regions refused to treat staff as subjects.

sentences.zh: 又異姓諸將居邊，宜參以親戚，而諸王公皆在京都，非扞城之義，萬世之固」。

translations.literal: Moreover various generals of other surnames hold the frontierlands—it is fitting to mix in kin; yet various princes and dukes all remain in the capital—not the meaning of defending walls or enduring fortification."
translations.idiomatic: Alien generals held borders while kin stayed in Luoyang—poor shield for the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝初未之察，於是下詔議其制。

translations.literal: The emperor at first did not examine it carefully; thereupon issued an edict ordering deliberation on the system.
translations.idiomatic: Wudi ordered debate before deciding.

sentences.zh: 有司奏，從諸王公更制戶邑，皆中尉領兵。

translations.literal: Responsible offices memorialized: follow various princes and dukes in revising household registrations—all middle commandants leading troops.
translations.idiomatic: Bureaus wanted princes refitted with armed middle commandants.

sentences.zh: 其平原、汝南、琅邪、扶風、齊為大國，梁、趙、樂安、燕、安平、義陽為次國，其餘為小國，皆制所近縣益滿萬戶。

translations.literal: Pingyuan, Runan, Langya, Fufeng, and Qi were large principalities; Liang, Zhao, Le'an, Yan, Anping, and Yiyang were middling; the rest were small—all regulations nearest counties augmented to fill ten thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: They tiered fiefs—five large, six middling—and topped up households.

sentences.zh: 又為郡公制度如小國王，亦中尉領兵。

translations.literal: Also for commandery-duke institutions like small princes—also middle commandants leading troops.
translations.idiomatic: County dukes mirrored small princes with armed commandants.

sentences.zh: 郡侯如不滿五千戶王，置一軍一千一百人，亦中尉領之。

translations.literal: Commandery marquis if not reaching five thousand households like a prince—establish one army eleven hundred men—also middle commandant leading.
translations.idiomatic: Smaller marquisates raised eleven hundred men under middle commandants.

sentences.zh: 于時，唯特增魯公國戶邑，追進封故司空博陵公王沈為郡公，钜平侯羊祜為南城郡侯。

translations.literal: At that time only Lu duke's registers were specially increased; posthumously advanced former Minister of Works Prince Boling Wang Shen to commandery duke; Julping marquis Yang Hu to southern-city commandery marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Only Lu gained extra households; Shen and Yang Hu were bumped posthumously.

sentences.zh: 又南宮王承、隨王萬各於泰始中封為縣王，邑千戶，至是改正縣王增邑為三千戶。

translations.literal: Also Prince Cheng of Nangong and Prince Wan of Sui had been made county princes in Taishi at one thousand households—now corrected county princes augmented households to three thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Taishi county princes jumped to three thousand households.

sentences.zh: 制度如郡侯，亦置一軍。

translations.literal: Institutions like commandery marquis—also establishing one army.
translations.idiomatic: County princes matched county marquis armies.

sentences.zh: 自此非皇子不得為王，而諸王之支庶，皆皇家之近屬至親，亦各以土推恩受封。

translations.literal: From this non-imperial sons could not be kings; yet various princes' lesser sons—all nearest imperial kin—each received fiefs by graded kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Only imperial sons could be kings; cadets took descending noble ranks.

sentences.zh: 其大國次國始封王之支子為公，承封王之支子為侯，繼承封王之支子為伯。

translations.literal: Large and middling principalities' first enfeoffed sons of kings became dukes; heirs of enfeoffed kings' sons became marquis; successors of heirs' sons became earls.
translations.idiomatic: Cadet ranks stepped down duke-marquis-earl by lineage tier.

sentences.zh: 小國五千戶已上，始封王之支子為子，不滿五千戶始封王之支子及始封公侯之支子皆為男，非此皆不得封。

translations.literal: Small principalities above five thousand households—first enfeoffed sons of kings became viscounts; below five thousand households first enfeoffed sons of kings and first enfeoffed sons of dukes and marquis all became barons—otherwise none could be enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: Small-fief cadets became viscounts or barons under household thresholds.

sentences.zh: 其公之制度如五千戶國，侯之制度如不滿五千戶國，亦置一軍千人，中尉領之，伯子男以下各有差而不置軍。

translations.literal: Duke institutions matched five-thousand-household principalities; marquis institutions matched sub-five-thousand principalities—also one army one thousand men led by middle commandant; earl, viscount, baron downward each graded downward without establishing armies.
translations.idiomatic: High nobles kept armies; lowest ranks had none.

sentences.zh: 大國始封之孫罷下軍，曾孫又罷上軍，次國始封子孫亦罷下軍，其餘皆以一軍為常。

translations.literal: Large principalities' first-enfeoffed grandsons abolished lower army; great-grandsons again abolished upper army; middling principalities' first-enfeoffed descendants also abolished lower army; the rest kept one army as norm.
translations.idiomatic: Succession trimmed armies generation by generation.

sentences.zh: 大國中軍二千人，上下軍各千五百人，次國上軍二千人，下軍千人。

translations.literal: Large principalities central army two thousand; upper and lower armies fifteen hundred each; middling principalities upper army two thousand; lower army one thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Troop floors matched principality tier.

sentences.zh: 其未之國者，大國置守土百人，次國八十人，小國六十人，郡侯縣公亦如小國制度。

translations.literal: Those not yet gone to fiefs—large principalities set one hundred homeland guards; middling eighty; small sixty; commandery marquis and county duke matched small principality institutions.
translations.idiomatic: Princes still in capital kept reduced household guards by size.

sentences.zh: 既行，所增徙各如本奏遣就國，而諸公皆戀京師，涕泣而去。

translations.literal: Once implemented, augmented relocations each as originally memorialized were dispatched to fiefs—yet various dukes all clung to the capital, weeping as they departed.
translations.idiomatic: Enforcement sent peers weeping from Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 及吳平後，齊王攸遂之國。

translations.literal: After Wu was pacified Prince You of Qi then went to his fief.
translations.idiomatic: After Wu fell Sima You finally left for his domain.

sentences.zh: 中朝制，典書令在常侍下，侍郎上。

translations.literal: Central court regulations—classics director ranked below standing attendant, above gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Capital ranks placed classics director between attendant and gentleman.

sentences.zh: 及渡江，則侍郎次常侍，而典書令居三軍下。

translations.literal: East of the Yangzi gentlemen ranked below standing attendant while classics director sat below the Three Armies office.
translations.idiomatic: South of the river reshuffled—gentlemen under attendants, classics director under three-armies.

sentences.zh: 公國則無中尉、常侍、三軍，侯國又無大農、侍郎，伯子男唯典書以下，又無學官、令史職，皆以次損焉。

translations.literal: Commandery dukes lacked middle commandant, standing attendant, Three Armies; marquis principalities lacked grand agronomist and gentleman; earls, viscounts, barons only classics directors downward—also no academy officers or clerks—each trimmed by grade.
translations.idiomatic: Lower noble seats shed offices stepwise.

sentences.zh: 公侯以下置官屬，隨國大小無定制，其餘官司各有差。

translations.literal: Dukes and marquis downward placed officials according to fief size without fixed pattern; remaining offices each differed.
translations.idiomatic: Staffing scaled loosely by fief.

sentences.zh: 名山大澤不以封，鹽鐵金銀銅錫，始平之竹園，別都宮室園囿，皆不為屬國。

translations.literal: Famous mountains and great marshes were not granted as fiefs; salt, iron, gold, silver, copper, tin, bamboo gardens at Shiping, detached-capital palaces and parks—none became dependent principalities.
translations.idiomatic: Strategic lands and mints stayed imperial.

sentences.zh: 其仕在天朝者，與之國同，皆自選其文武官。

translations.literal: Those serving in the celestial court matched those in fiefs—all chose their own civil and military officers.
translations.idiomatic: Capital nobles picked staff like those in the provinces.

sentences.zh: 諸入作卿士而其世子年已壯者，皆遣蒞國。

translations.literal: Various men appointed capital ministers whose heir sons were already adult—all were sent to oversee fiefs.
translations.idiomatic: Adult heirs had to take seats in their domains.

sentences.zh: 其王公已下，茅社符璽，車旗命服，一如泰始初故事。

translations.literal: From dukes downward—thatched altars, tallies and seals, carriage banners and mandated dress—all followed Taishi founding precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Noble regalia matched Taishi inaugural rules.

sentences.zh: 州置刺史，別駕、治中從事、諸曹從事等員。

translations.literal: Provinces set inspectors, aide-de-camp, administrative clerks, various bureau clerks, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: Each province ran inspectors with aides and bureau staff.

sentences.zh: 所領中郡以上及江陽、硃提郡，郡各置部從事一人，小郡亦置一人。

translations.literal: Among commanded interior commanderies upward plus Jiangyang and Zhuti commanderies—each commandery placed one division clerk; small commanderies also placed one.
translations.idiomatic: Interior commanderies gained division clerks.

sentences.zh: 又有主簿，門亭長、錄事、記室書佐、諸曹佐、守從事、武猛從事等。

translations.literal: Also chief clerk, gate precinct chief, recorder, secretary clerks, various bureau assistants, guard clerks, fierce clerks, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: Plus clerks, recorders, and bailiffs.

sentences.zh: 凡吏四十一人，卒二十人。

translations.literal: In all forty-one clerks and twenty runners.
translations.idiomatic: Forty-one clerks and twenty runners standard.

sentences.zh: 諸州邊遠，或有山險，濱近寇賊羌夷者，又置弓馬從事五十餘人。

translations.literal: Various provinces far away or with mountain hazards or bordering bandits, Qiang, and Yi—also placed fifty-some bow-and-horse clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier provinces added mounted archer aides.

sentences.zh: 徐州又置淮海，涼州置河津，諸州置都水從事各一人。

translations.literal: Xuzhou additionally set Huaihai; Liangzhou set river-ford; various provinces each set one water-affairs clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Xuzhou took Huaihai aides; Liangzhou river crossing; others water clerks.

sentences.zh: 涼、益州置吏八十五人，卒二十人。

translations.literal: Liang and Yi provinces placed eighty-five clerks and twenty runners.
translations.idiomatic: Liang and Yi ran eighty-five clerks.

sentences.zh: 荊州又置監佃督一人。

translations.literal: Jingzhou additionally set one colony overseer.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhou added a colony superintendent.

sentences.zh: 郡皆置太守，河南郡京師所在，則曰尹。

translations.literal: Commanderies all set grand wardens; Henan commandery where the capital sat was called intendant.
translations.idiomatic: Commanderies used 'warden' except Henan 'intendant.'

sentences.zh: 諸王國以內史掌太守之任，又置主簿、主記室、門下賊曹、議生、門下史、記室史、錄事史、書佐、循行、幹、小史、五官掾、功曹史、功曹書佐、循行小史、五官掾等員。

translations.literal: Various princely kingdoms used interior stewards to hold grand warden duty; also chief clerk, chief secretary, gate thieves office, deliberation students, gate clerks, secretary clerks, recorder clerks, document clerks, patrol runners, clerks, petty clerks, gatekeeper officers, merit clerks, merit clerk assistants, patrol petty clerks, gatekeeper officers, and other seats.
translations.idiomatic: Princely kingdoms mirrored commanderies with interior stewards and full clerical roster.

sentences.zh: 郡國戶不滿五千者，置職吏五十人，散吏十三人；

translations.literal: Commanderies and kingdoms below five thousand households placed fifty duty clerks and thirteen supernumerary clerks;
translations.idiomatic: Under five thousand households: fifty duty and thirteen extra clerks;

sentences.zh: 五千戶以上，則職吏六十三人，散吏二十一人；

translations.literal: above five thousand households then sixty-three duty clerks and twenty-one supernumerary clerks;
translations.idiomatic: above five thousand: sixty-three duty and twenty-one supernumerary;

sentences.zh: 萬戶以上，職吏六十九人，散吏三十九人。

translations.literal: above ten thousand households—sixty-nine duty clerks and thirty-nine supernumerary clerks.
translations.idiomatic: above ten thousand: sixty-nine duty and thirty-nine supernumerary.

sentences.zh: 郡國皆置文學掾一人。

translations.literal: Commanderies and kingdoms all placed one literary clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Every commandery kept a literary aide.

sentences.zh: 縣大者置令，小者置長。

translations.literal: Large counties placed magistrates; small counties placed chiefs.
translations.idiomatic: Big districts got magistrates; small ones got chiefs.

sentences.zh: 有主簿、錄事史、主記室史、門下書佐、幹、遊徼、議生、循行功曹史、小史、廷掾、功曹史、小史書佐幹、戶曹掾史幹、法曹門幹、金倉賊曹掾史、兵曹史、吏曹史、獄小史、獄門亭長、都亭長、賊捕掾等員。

translations.literal: There were chief clerks, recorder clerks, chief secretary clerks, gate document clerks, clerks, patrol inspectors, deliberation students, patrol merit clerks, petty clerks, court clerks, merit clerks, petty clerk document clerks, household bureau clerks and clerks, law bureau gate clerks, metals-granary-thieves bureau clerks, military bureau clerks, personnel bureau clerks, prison petty clerks, prison gate precinct chiefs, capital precinct chiefs, thieves-capture clerks, and other seats.
translations.idiomatic: County offices stacked chief clerks through precinct bailiffs—full fiscal and legal desks.

sentences.zh: 戶不滿三百以下，職吏十八人，散吏四人；

translations.literal: Households below three hundred—eighteen duty clerks, four supernumerary clerks;
translations.idiomatic: Under three hundred households: eighteen duty and four extra clerks;

sentences.zh: 三百以上，職吏二十八人，散吏六人；

translations.literal: above three hundred—twenty-eight duty clerks, six supernumerary clerks;
translations.idiomatic: above three hundred: twenty-eight duty and six extra;

sentences.zh: 五百以上，職吏四十人，散吏八人；

translations.literal: above five hundred—forty duty clerks, eight supernumerary clerks;
translations.idiomatic: above five hundred: forty duty and eight extra;

sentences.zh: 千以上，職吏五十三人，散吏十二人；

translations.literal: above one thousand—fifty-three duty clerks, twelve supernumerary clerks;
translations.idiomatic: above one thousand: fifty-three duty and twelve extra;

sentences.zh: 千五百以上，職吏六十八人，散吏一十八人；

translations.literal: above fifteen hundred—sixty-eight duty clerks, eighteen supernumerary clerks;
translations.idiomatic: above fifteen hundred: sixty-eight duty and eighteen extra;

sentences.zh: 三千以上，職吏八十八人，散吏二十六人。

translations.literal: above three thousand—eighty-eight duty clerks, twenty-six supernumerary clerks.
translations.idiomatic: above three thousand: eighty-eight duty and twenty-six extra.

sentences.zh: 郡國及縣，農月皆隨所領戶多少為差，散吏為勸農。

translations.literal: Commanderies, kingdoms, and counties—in farming months all followed registered households in graded differences; supernumerary clerks served as farming encouragers.
translations.idiomatic: Planting season scaled clerks to household counts; extras promoted agriculture.

sentences.zh: 又縣五百以上皆置鄉，三千以上置二鄉，五千以上置三鄉，萬以上置四鄉，鄉置嗇夫一人。

translations.literal: Also counties above five hundred households all placed townships; above three thousand placed two townships; above five thousand placed three townships; above ten thousand placed four townships—each township placed one bailiff.
translations.idiomatic: Townships scaled with population—each run by a bailiff.

sentences.zh: 鄉戶不滿千以下，置治書史一人；

translations.literal: Townships below one thousand households placed one law-editing clerk;
translations.idiomatic: Small townships added one law clerk;

sentences.zh: 千以上置史、佐各一人，正一人；

translations.literal: above one thousand placed clerk and assistant one each, rectifier one;
translations.idiomatic: larger townships added clerk, assistant, and rectifier;

sentences.zh: 五千五百以上，置史一人，佐二人。

translations.literal: above fifty-five hundred placed one clerk, two assistants.
translations.idiomatic: above fifty-five hundred: one clerk and two assistants.

sentences.zh: 縣率百戶置裏吏一人，其土廣人稀，聽隨宜置裏吏，限不得減五十戶。

translations.literal: Counties normally placed one hamlet clerk per hundred households; where land was broad and people sparse, hamlet clerks were placed as suitable—limited to no fewer than fifty households.
translations.idiomatic: Hamlet overseers averaged one per hundred households but flexed in sparse terrain—never below fifty households.

sentences.zh: 戶千以上，置校官掾一人。

translations.literal: Above one thousand households placed one school clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Thousand-household counties gained an academy clerk.

sentences.zh: 縣皆置方略吏四人。

translations.literal: All counties placed four strategy clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Every county kept four strategy aides.

sentences.zh: 洛陽縣置六部尉。

translations.literal: Luoyang county placed six division captains.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang ran six ward captains.

sentences.zh: 江左以後，建康亦置六部尉，餘大縣置二人，次縣、小縣各一人。

translations.literal: East of the Yangzi afterward Jiankang also placed six division captains; other large counties placed two; middling and small counties one each.
translations.idiomatic: Jiankang mirrored Luoyang's six wards; other counties used one or two.

sentences.zh: 鄴、長安置吏如三千戶以上之制。

translations.literal: Ye and Chang'an placed clerks according to above-three-thousand-household regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Ye and Chang'an staffed at the three-thousand tier.

sentences.zh: 四中郎將，並後漢置，曆魏及晉，並有其職，江左彌重。

translations.literal: Four gentlemen-of-the-palace generals—all Later Han established; through Wei and Jin the posts existed; east of the Yangzi they grew weightier.
translations.idiomatic: The four palace generals survived Han through Jin and mattered more in the south.

sentences.zh: 護羌、夷、蠻等校尉，案武帝置南蠻校尉于襄陽，西戎校尉于長安，南夷校尉于甯州。

translations.literal: Qiang, Yi, Man protectors-general—in tradition Emperor Wu placed Southern Man protector-general at Xiangyang, Western Rong protector-general at Chang'an, Southern Yi protector-general at Ningzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wudi posted barbarian commissioners—south at Xiangyang, west at Chang'an, Yi at Ning.

sentences.zh: 元康中，護羌校尉為涼州刺史，西戎校尉為雍州刺史，南蠻校尉為荊州刺史。

translations.literal: During Yuankang Qiang protector-general became Liangzhou inspector; Western Rong protector-general became Yongzhou inspector; Southern Man protector-general became Jingzhou inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Yuankang folded commissioners into provincial inspectors—Qiang into Liang, Rong into Yong, Man into Jing.

sentences.zh: 及江左初，省南蠻校尉，尋又置於江陵，改南夷校尉曰鎮蠻校尉。

translations.literal: Early east of the Yangzi Southern Man protector-general was cut; soon restored at Jiangling; Southern Yi protector-general was renamed Pacification Man protector-general.
translations.idiomatic: South of the river Man posts flickered; Jiangling revived them; Yi commissioner became 'pacify Man.'

sentences.zh: 及安帝時，于襄陽置甯蠻校尉。

translations.literal: When Emperor An ruled, Pacification Man protector-general was placed at Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Andi added a pacification commissioner at Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 護匈奴、羌、戎、蠻、夷、越中郎將，案武帝置四中郎將，或領刺史，或持節為之。

translations.literal: Xiongnu, Qiang, Rong, Man, Yi, Yue gentlemen-of-the-palace generals—in tradition Emperor Wu established four gentlemen-of-the-palace generals—some concurrently inspectors, some credential-bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Wudi's four palace generals doubled as governors or credential holders for tribes.

sentences.zh: 武帝又置平越中郎將，居廣州，主護南越。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu also established Pacification Yue gentleman-of-the-palace general, residing at Guangzhou, chiefly protecting Southern Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Wudi added a Yue pacification general at Guangzhou for the far south.
